News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

Sports.title: Who will win title? Will Max leave Red Bull? - Key questions as F1 returns
Sports.content:
Formula 1's summer break is over and the 2026 season restarts in the Netherlands this weekend as the championship run-in looms over the final months of the campaign.

We asked Sky Sports F1 pundit Karun Chandhok to run the rule over some of the key questions left to be answered on and off track this year and predict how things might pan out from here…

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See what some of the Formula 1 drivers, including Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, got up to during the summer break!

How many drivers still have a realistic title shot?

Kimi Antonelli's 50-point championship lead puts him firmly in the hunt, but fewer points cover Lewis Hamilton in second down to Lando Norris, the winner of the last race in Hungary, in fifth. With two Sprints and up to 12 Grands Prix to go, there are potentially as many as 316 points left to play for between now and December.

Karun says: "I think, realistically, this is Antonelli's championship to lose. Nobody has come back from this big a points deficit since we went to this scoring system in 2010. Kimi is driving well, he has got a lot of confidence in the car and the way it's working for him.

"The only Achilles' heel seems to be Mercedes' reliability. That could be a challenge, but they are going to keep improving that. So realistically, I think it is his championship to lose, which is an extraordinary achievement in just his second year in F1.

"The only thing I would say is, with the way the upgrades and updates are going, it will be interesting to see what Ferrari can do, and also whether any of Mercedes' upgrades help George Russell out, because it does feel like he has had obviously more bad luck but also a pace disadvantage this year.

"I think it is only Lewis or maybe George who could challenge him, but it's more his to lose."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the Formula 1 season set to resume after the summer break, we look back at how Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has built a 50-point lead in the driver standings.

Which team is the one to watch for development?

In-season car development is always crucial in Formula 1 but the stakes have been raised this year with teams still in the early stages of understanding how to unlock the best performance from the all-new 2026 aerodynamic rules and engines. The first half of the season saw teams make big jumps in performance at races they brought update packages, and others did not, with that trend expected to continue after the summer break.

Karun says: "I'm interested to see what McLaren do. Clearly the car was very good in Budapest and that bodes well for the Dutch Grand Prix because whoever is good in Budapest should have a good car for Zandvoort.

"And they've got more bits coming this weekend on the rear end of the car as well, which is the second half of the update.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

"The big one to keep an eye out for is Red Bull, because they have been a bit more inconsistent and there's a bit of a battle on for them to play catch-up.

"If you look at it across the season, they have had the fourth-fastest car, which is not ideal in terms of trying to keep Max happy and at the team.

"So, Red Bull are the ones I'm most interested in watching out for to see if they can dig themselves out of this hole in terms of inconsistencies."

Where will Max Verstappen end up driving for 2027?

The big question on which the volatility of the driver market hinges. Max Verstappen is contracted to Red Bull until the end of 2028 but a position outside the top two of the Drivers' Championship at the summer break - he sits in sixth place - means he is free to activate a break clause in the deal for the end of this year, should he wish. The answer to the question of whether he will or not remains unknown with Verstappen thought to have until October to tell Red Bull should he want to leave. Immediate alternative options for him for 2027, however, should he want to continue in F1 remain uncertain despite links to McLaren and Mercedes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive Max Verstappen's troublesome 2026 season, with the Red Bull driver having suffered multiple issues.

Karun says: "I have no idea when Max will end up driving in 2027 but I think realistically, I don't think he knows yet either.

"I think he is waiting to see where the Red Bull goes and really what other options there are."

Will Fernando Alonso race on or retire from F1 for 2027?

Fernando Alonso said he would use the summer break to decide on whether he will extend his F1 career into a record-extending 24th campaign next season. The Spaniard, who turned 45 in July and became a father for the first time earlier this year, has downplayed suggestions his decision completely rests on how competitive he expects Aston Martin to be in 2027, saying that it will also be influenced on how he feels about the sport's current rules.

Karun says: "I think if Aston can demonstrate that they are going to make progress and Honda can demonstrate that they are making progress and they can give Alonso a car that at least gets him into Q3 and gives him something to fight for in 2027, then he will stick around.

"He is not going to stick around to be someone who gets knocked out in Q1 all the time."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso said Aston Martin’s new upgrades delivered improvements in Hungary.

How high will Aston Martin get up the grid?

The clear underperformer of the season's first half after all manner of issues with their 2026 chassis and Honda engine left them at the back of the grid, Aston Martin delivered what they hope will provide the first of many steps forward with their first car upgrade last time out in Hungary. Further revisions to Adrian Newey's AMR26 and the first long-awaited engine upgrade, which is set to arrive at Zandvoort, offer the potential for further progress heading towards 2027.

Karun says: "Aston Martin have got to get themselves in a position where they need to end this year at least occasionally getting into Q3 because that then lays the foundation for 2027 and beyond.

"The engine upgrades will be critical for that. If you look at their straight-line speed at Spa, it was shocking. They brought the updated chassis to Budapest and that seemed to give them some performance advantage, a decent step.

"So really with the engine advantage, they might occasionally sneak themselves into Q3, which would be good progress but more importantly, a good foundation."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the last Formula One race coming up at Zandvoort, look back at some of the most dramatic moments throughout the years at the Dutch Grand Prix.

How many drivers will win races over the remaining rounds?

F1 broke for summer on a run of five different winners in as many races with both Mercedes drivers, both Ferrari drivers and McLaren's Lando Norris standing on the top step of the podium during that run.

Karun says: "I think there is a chance we could see both Ferrari drivers, McLaren drivers and Mercedes drivers winning races, and Max.

"If Red Bull do upgrade well and bring good bits and pieces, then we could see Max winning. He wasn't that far off in Austria, and the car steadily made progress. They need a couple of jumps and they could do it."

What will Sepang be like on F1's return and who might the track favour?

For the first time in nine years, F1 will race at the much-loved Sepang International Circuit in October after Malaysia agreed to host the Bahrain Grand Prix. Sepang built a reputation as both a driver and fan favourite across its 18 years on the calendar, with the track featuring challenging corner combinations and providing good racing.

Karun says: "I love Sepang. I first raced there in 2001, which was my first year of international racing. I've been back in lots of different categories and have always absolutely loved the circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Formula 1 has added Malaysia to its 2026 schedule to host the Bahrain Grand Prix that was postponed earlier in the season.

"I think it is a really interesting, challenging layout, good for racing. I'm delighted to see everyone going back there, albeit temporarily.

"I think we are going to see a fantastic race. For this year's cars, there are plenty of opportunities to harvest and recharge the batteries and energy around chunks of the lap, so it should be a pretty good race all round.

"It is going to be hot, so anyone who can keep the tyre temperatures under control will be in good shape."

Who will win the 2026 championships?

Antonelli's half-century lead at mid-season makes him the clear bookmakers' favourite ahead of Lewis Hamilton and George Russell, who was most people's tips for the title at the start of the year.

Mercedes would likely have been away and clear already and not just 72 points ahead of Ferrari had they not suffered from reliability problems. Nonetheless, Ferrari outscored them in each of the three races before the summer break and, with reliability on their side, aren't to be ruled out yet. McLaren were 78 points back on Red Bull with 12 races to go in 2024 and ended up as champions.

Karun says: "I think this is Antonelli's drivers' title to lose, and Mercedes' Constructors' Championship to lose."

The Formula 1 season resumes after the summer break with a Sprint weekend at the Dutch Grand Prix from Friday, with every session live on Sky Sports. Stream Sky Sports with NOW - no contract, cancel anytime

Sports.title: Kevin Blake's York tips: Ebor Festival day two picks
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing’s Kevin Blake reveals a trio of picks as York's Ebor Festival rolls on into day two on Thursday.

The Ebor Festival at York rolls on into day two on Thursday and while the main events will provide world-class action for us to enjoy, it is the supporting card that might well offer the best betting opportunities.

The Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 In 7 Grand Finale Handicap (3:00) is yet another brutally-tough handicap puzzle to solve, but William Haggas may have the answer in the shape of BULLET POINT. The five-year-old won this race last year off a mark of 100, enjoying a smooth trip around from a good draw and winning with some authority.

However, his career hasn't continued on the upward curve as might have been expected since then, with a trip down to Australia ending in disappointment followed by a six-month absence. Since his return, it wouldn't be at all surprising if his connections have been working backwards from this race.

He shaped with subtle promise in two runs in valuable handicaps earlier this season and then returned from another 12 weeks off to run a fine race in defeat at the Shergar Cup, finding just one that had got loose on the lead too good for him. He gets to run off the same mark of 101 here and while the draw hasn't been quite so good to him this year as it was last year, he still looks to have leading prospects.

The next contest of interest is the Mews Hotel Ossett EBF Stallions Nursery (4:45). Three weeks ago, this column put up the Hugo Palmer-trained MIA FANTASIA in a valuable nursery at Glorious Goodwood. To say he had a troubled passage would be underselling it! He got next to no luck in running and shaped much better than the bare result.

The case that made for him that day remains relevant, with him having overcome his inexperience to win in good style at Carlisle on debut before not quite being sharp enough to be as competitive in what has proven to be a smart novice contest at Ascot that was won by the subsequent Vintage Stakes winner Dr Rascal. A mark of 79 seems very fair indeed and he is sure to have benefited from the experience he gained at Goodwood. He looks likely to run a big race.

The final race of interest on the day is another very tough handicap, the British EBF Fillies' Handicap (5:20). Again, cases can be made for so many of these, but I'm going to venture down towards the bottom end of the weights and side with the Ed Walker-trained SECRET HISTORY.

The three-year-old has already won three times this year, with her most notable victory coming in a valuable seven-furlong handicap at Newmarket in July. Raised 4lb for that, her connections took a chance in dropping her to six furlongs to contest a valuable fillies' handicap at Glorious Goodwood and while she ran well to finish third, she shaped as though the test was sharper than ideal for her. Returning to this trip will be a big help to her and she looks to have very strong prospects.

Sports.title: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory
Sports.content:
Item delivered for Andrew Balding and the sponsors to land a 10-1 surprise in the Juddmonte International at York – with the big two of Constitution River and Ombudsman only third and fourth respectively.

Hawk Mountain rather unexpectedly set the early pace, with stablemate Constitution River tucked in keenly behind him and odds-on favourite Ombudsman at the rear under William Buick, kept company by another Aidan O'Brien runner, Action.

Hawk Mountain was still in front as they moved to the top of the long Knavesmire straight, with Buick beginning to make headway on the inside rail, as Ryan Moore and Constitution River kicked for home over two furlongs out.

Ombudsman kept making ground on the inside, but the dangers were coming on the outside and it was Ed Walker's Almaqam who pulled away with half a furlong to run, only for Item to arrive in full flight, just getting his head down on the line in the hands of Colin Keane.

Balding has now achieved something his later father, Ian, the trainer of Mill Reef, never managed. He said: "I don't think he had many goes at it, though, in fairness. It's always one of the most important races of the year. So it's lovely to win it with a horse like this.

"We've pitched him in some good races with the belief that he will do well in them, but he's kept improving and improved physically. That's the most important thing.

"He's really a very different horse than the one that ran in the Dante, physically."

He added: "I think anything is possible, he certainly has no problem staying a mile and a half if he wanted to.

"I just want to say a big thank you to the team at home because it wasn't straightforward getting him here. Everything had gone great up until about declaration time and we had a little hiccup there with his feet.

"Thankfully everyone who looks after him have worked overtime to get it right, and happily it was a 5am decision that he got on the box to come up here. I'm very relieved."

On Item's next assignment, the Kingsclere handler said: "I just do not know at this moment in time. I think we've got to sit down and let the dust settle. We've just won a Juddmonte International, that was the plan."

Sports.title: Doyle: King George heroine 'too hot' for Oaks field
Sports.content:
Our ambassador returns to preview the second day of the Ebor Festival at York on Thursday, covering a variety of Group, Handicap and Listed events.

Kalpana too hot for Minnie in Yorkshire Oaks

Kalpana, a brilliant winner of the King George last month, will prove too hot for Minnie Hauk to handle in Thursday's showstopper at York, the Group One Legends Global Yorkshire Oaks (3.35).

The great French horse Calandagan simply had no answer to Andrew Balding's mare at Ascot, where Aidan O'Brien's multiple Oaks winner finished a disappointing 18 lengths adrift.

That was the second time in a row Minnie Hauk has put in an underwhelming performance and I just can't see her re-capturing her best form in time to bridge that yawning gap. Back against her own sex, Kalpana is simply irresistible, even if the forecast rain arrives.

At bigger odds, I hope to see David Menuisier's Inis Mor maintain the progress that has seen her make the frame in both the French and Irish Oaks. This is tougher still, but Oisin Murphy knows how to get the best out of her.

Irish filly ready to step into Pattern company

Juddmonte's Irish-trained filly Livenka looks ready to stamp her class on the Group Two Sky Bet Lowther Stakes (1.50) at York on Thursday.

Ger Lyons' daughter of Bated Breath booked her place in this line-up by taking a valuable sales race at Naas by nearly four lengths, suggesting she's ready to step into Pattern company.

She's drawn high but isn't far away from the probable favourite Libertango, the Albany winner who only narrowly lost her unbeaten record in the Group Two Duchess Of Cambridge at Newmarket.

George Boughey's filly sets the standard, but Livenka arrives on an upward curve and looks too smart to ignore, while Andrew Balding's Moonrise is another big player. She was second in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot before winning the Princess Margaret yet has been largely overlooked in the Ante-post markets.

Oaks fourth stands out in Galtres

My husband Tom (Marquand) and his boss William Haggas can expect a big run from Rhapsody in the British EBF & Sir Henry Cecil Galtres Stakes (4.10) at York - but she has one filly in particular to be fearful of.

Rhapsody brings ideal credentials to this Listed race with a Group placing and a course win to her name. However, I'm expecting Ralph Backett's A La Prochaine to take full advantage of this drop-in class.

Still lightly raced, she ran well in the Cheshire Oaks in the spring but stepped forward again to be fourth in the Oaks itself at Epsom on her latest start. She's been freshened up since then and looks a much sounder proposition than the likely favourite Morrophore, who's best form has been achieved on the All-Weather. She must also overcome an eight-month absence.

Satellite the value in big sales dash

It's pretty unusual to see a Group One winner in a sales race but the participation of Sun Goddess in the Harry's Half Million By Goffs (2.25) at York demonstrates the limitless strength in depth at Ballydoyle.

Aidan O'Brien's Phoenix Stakes heroine looks thrown in on these terms and will probably go off an even shorter priced favourite if her Albany victor Libertango wins the Lowther.

Still, anything can happen in big-field sales races so there has to be some value in Clive Cox's unbeaten Satellite Of Love, who has over a stone to find with Sun Goddess but has a plum low draw and a progressive profile to go with it.

She really impressed me in her Newbury novice while I am also keeping an eye out for my boss Archie Watson's game filly Vollering, who has already picked up valuable black type in France and has plenty of experience now.

Bullet Point ready to follow up big Handicap

Bullet Point came back to form in timely fashion in this month's Shergar Cup and can go one better in the Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 In 7 Grand Finale Handicap (3.00) at York.

Last year's winner was clearly transformed by the first-time cheekpieces at Ascot and looks another winning chance for Tom (Marquand) if the headgear proves as effective a second time.

Ralph Beckett's Ante-post favourite Centigrade looks short enough for a horse stepping out of an All-Weather novice but I'd like to see Jack Channon's Mezcala involved at the business end of the race. The Buckingham Palace winner hasn't been blessed with the best of draws in stall 17 but will enjoy York if he gets that all-important luck in running.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Fisher opponent revealed ahead of Copper Box return
Sports.content:
Johnny Fisher's opponent has been confirmed as Michael Pirotton ahead of the eagerly awaited return of the 'Romford Bull' next month.

The British heavyweight (14-1, 12 KOs) makes his Zuffa Boxing debut against Belgium's Pirotton in the 10-round main event, live on Sky Sports on Saturday, September 26.

Fisher ended the year with a stoppage win over Ivan Balaz in December, putting his career back on track after a rematch loss to David Allen in May.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher says he is inspired by his 'Bosh Army' and has his eyes set on fighting for the British title very soon

Pirotton (12-2, 6 KOs) lies in wait next, with Fisher telling Sky Sports: "I'm excited, but I'm also driven and determined.

"The next fight is always the hardest fight, and everyone I fight is a dangerous opponent because they're getting onto this show with Sky Sports, Zufa, with the Romford Bull Army there.

"It's a golden ticket for Michael Pirotton, but it's also my golden ticket because if I win, I get to go on to bigger and better things. I've got ambitions in this game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher reveals what Chinese takeaway order he would get for co-founder of Zuffa Boxing Dana White

Pirotton made his professional debut in 2019 and won his first 10 fights. After dropping a pair of decisions to unbeaten foes in 2025, he rebounded this year with two stoppage victories.

He has never previously been knocked down, but Fisher is hoping to change that.

"You want to get the knockout, you want to get the stoppage, but I've always said from the beginning of my career, I've got to win by whatever cost - the win is the most important thing." he said.

"But with my power, my strength, my explosivity, of course I can draw a knockout or draw a stoppage.

"Once I get someone hurt, I know I can finish them. I can smell when someone's feeling it or in trouble.

Fisher added: "I'm very very excited to show people what I can do. You haven't seen the best version of the Romford Bull yet. We're going to try and show that on September 26."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lee Cutler and Louis Greene had an intense face-off as their fight was announced on Sky Sports News for Zuffa Boxing 11 in September

Fisher vs. Pirotton tops a bill that also features a 10-round light heavyweight co-main event between Craig "Spider" Richards, Radivoje "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic, and British middleweights Lee Cutler (16-2, 8 KOs) and Louis Greene (19-4, 12 KOs) squaring off in a 10-rounder.

Welterweight Alex MacMillan (4-0, 3 KOs) and light heavyweight Leon Hughes (5-0, 4 KOs) will see action in separate six-rounders, while lightweights Kayla Allen and Fred Pullen will make their respective professional debuts.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree £51m deal to sign Aston Villa's Konsa
Sports.content:
Arsenal have agreed a £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

The Premier League champions have been looking for a new defender with William Saliba out for an extended period of time and Jurrien Timber also sidelined with a long-term groin problem.

Arsenal looked into a potential deal for Bayer Leverkusen's Jarell Quansah but have chosen to advance with a move for his England team-mate Konsa. Both players have a similar profile and can play at right-back and centre-back.

Villa had initially held out for £60m, with Arsenal hoping to pay much less, but the two clubs found a compromise on Thursday to strike a deal for the 28-year-old.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan brings the latest on Ezri Konsa, as Arsenal agree a deal with Aston Villa for the defender.

Konsa must be registered by midday on Thursday to be available for Arsenal's Premier League opener against Coventry, live on Sky Sports, on Friday.

If not ready for this weekend, Konsa could make his Premier League debut for Arsenal at Aston Villa, live on Sky Sports' Monday Night Football on August 31.

Villa, meanwhile, have an interest in Tosin Adarabioyo at Chelsea as a potential replacement for Konsa.

Chelsea are now ready to listen to offers for Tosin, who also has interest from Marseille, Benfica and Sevilla.

Arsenal

Coventry City Friday 21st August 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

Analysis: Konsa is a perfect Arteta player - here's why

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

If there's one thing you need to know about Mikel Arteta, it's that he loves players that win duels. Nobody was better at it than Ezri Konsa last season.

The England international won more duels on the ground than any other Premier League player last season - finishing quite some distance ahead of his nearest challengers Virgil van Dijk and Gabriel - who looks set to be his team-mate next season.

Image: Konsa had the best ground duel success rate out of any Premier League defender last season

Arsenal are in need of defensive reinforcement this summer with both William Saliba and Jurrien Timber both out injured, so need a player who can cover both right-back and centre-back roles.

The Gunners do have Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White as cover in those roles - and both performed well in the Community Shield win over Manchester City - but the latter has a difficult injury record over the last two seasons.

Arsenal also saw the importance of having good depth at right-back when Mosquera was forced to start the Champions League final with PSG out of position - which then resulted in the young Spaniard conceding a penalty.

Should a move for Konsa be completed, Arsenal have filled an important part of their team - and would be very close to completing their transfer window from an incomings point of view.

Can they find the forward player they have been looking the whole window for?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett talks to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta about the club having the 'ambition and desire' to win back-to-back Premier League titles and how they are targeting elite players to be the best club in the world

Arteta is excited to keep building Arsenal after their Premier League win, vowing to make them "the best club in the world".

"It's certainly the ambition of the club and the owners to be the best club in the world," he told Sky Sports at a Premier League launch event ahead of their Friday night opener against Coventry, live on Sky.

"In order to do that, you need the best facilities, the best stadium, the best supporters, and you need the best squad and the best players in the world.

"Those are the ones that win you football matches and the ones that can be decisive when it matters.

"That's what we try to build with the actual players that we have, and with the players that we want to sign to make the difference for Arsenal."

Arsenal go into the season as outright favourites to retain their title, with that status further underlined by their comfortable 3-0 win over Manchester City in Sunday's Community Shield. Arteta, however, says he is more than comfortable with the position of being the frontrunners.

"This is part of our industry, and that's okay," he said. "For me, it's when I look into the eyes of my players and I see that fire, that desire and the will to be better every single day. That's the only thing that I care about."

The weight of history is against Arsenal defending their trophy, however. Arsenal have not defended the top-flight title since the 1930s. It is another milestone Arteta is keen to overcome.

"That's an opportunity that we have ahead, and we are very conscious of what it's going to take to deliver that," he said. "But I feel the ambition, I feel the desire, and I feel the ability and the conviction around the team that we can do it."

Sports.title: Referees’ chief Howard Webb ‘really troubled’ by Folarin Balogun escaping World Cup ban
Sports.content:
Howard Webb was “really troubled” by the decision of Fifa’s disciplinary committee to suspend Folarin Balogun’s ban for a red card during the World Cup, warning of a growing belief in refereeing conspiracies among supporters. Webb, English football’s chief refereeing officer, was speaking before the new Premier League season, where, among a series of new measures, independent assessments of key refereeing decisions are to be made public for the first time.

“I was really troubled by it,” Webb said of the reprieve for the USA striker Balogun, which followed a direct appeal from the US president, Donald Trump. “What do we know? We know for sure that a red card was shown. I understand why it was given. We know that there was pressure placed by a politician on to Fifa, because that was admitted. And we know that the suspension was taken away for that particular tournament and suspended through a process which seemingly didn’t exist before the tournament started.”

Webb said the scandal would only reinforce a change that has already taken place, whereby spectators watch a referee make a mistake and see conspiracy rather than human error. “We live in a world now which is different to the one that I occupied as a referee,” he said. “Decisions were previously viewed as correct or incorrect, based on your judgment. Far too often now decisions are viewed as correct or corrupt by people who want to type all over social media. They try to draw inferences around decisions that they don’t agree with and draw a motivation behind that decision which is borne out of no facts, no evidence.”

Webb’s feelings on the Balogun scandal were echoed by the chief executive of the Premier League, Richard Masters. “We should be talking about looking back on the World Cup and the football that was played, and Spain being obviously the best team and England’s agonising semi-final defeat,” Masters said. “We’re not. We’re talking about other issues. I think that’s a huge shame. The Balogun issue … is very difficult to comprehend really when you look at it.”

View image in fullscreen Howard Webb said the game had changed since he was a referee. Photograph: Zac Goodwin/PA

English football’s refereeing body has announced a series of measures and targets for the new season, including a rebrand. Now known as Pro Ref, it has committed to publish each week the assessments of an independent key match incident (KMI) panel, which assesses the biggest decisions taken by Premier League referees. As reported by the Guardian, Pro Ref will also publish audio of conversations between referees and players during matches, and it will continue to use X to publish real-time information during games.

Pro Ref has expanded the pool of specialist video assistant referees working at Stockley Park as it seeks to reduce the length of time taken on interventions – which averaged 41 seconds last season – and eliminate incidents where VARs intervene and should not. “I’d rather have missed interventions than over-interventions,” Webb said. “I’d rather VAR not get involved wrongly to rectify something that wasn’t wrong in the first place, because that’s a damaging effect on the game.” In a further attempt to improve the speed of decision-making, the protocol behind semi-automatic offside technology has also been streamlined.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Webb said fans and players alike can also expect to see more penalties awarded for holding at set pieces. “More situations will be penalised, not only in August or September, but throughout the season,” Webb said. “[But] I’m not going to commit to say we’re going to go from here to penalising lots of contact. Contact is still part of the game, we still maintain a high threshold, but this time next year, all being well, we’ll be able to reflect on a season where more offences have been penalised.”

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 16: Manchester United
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 5th (NB: this is not necessarily Jamie Jackson’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd

Prospects

The information at the start of the close season was that Manchester United planned to trade for bargains rather than elite names and the major purchases so far this summer prove this to indeed be the case. Youri Tielemans is a 29-year-old who has been a professional for nearly half of his life and was bought, with no competition, for his £35m release clause from Aston Villa. The midfielder was followed by the £48m (+£2m) purchase of Andrey Santos, a 22-year-old with 11 league starts last season for Chelsea. The Brazilian states a preference for operating “deep, like a No 6” making him the direct replacement for his compatriot Casemiro, whose CV includes five Champions Leagues. United are also set to sign another midfielder in Carlos Baleba from Brighton for around £75m.

Michael Carrick, going in to his first full season in charge, admits his squad needs more additions and a new left-back is on the radar. Lewis Hall is the prime target but Newcastle’s resistance to a sale means Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly had drawn interest. At the window’s commencement, Carrick wanted Elliot Anderson but this was unrealistic – he went to City for around £32m more than Tielemans’ and Santos’s combined fee. Confirmed as manager in May after guiding United to third, Carrick may rue Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s reluctance to invest the finances he generated by taking the club back into the Champions League and the 45-year-old may find himself engulfed in precisely what has plagued all of his predecessors in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era: a crisis of performances and results.

Carrick also has to wrestle with the Marcus Rashford situation: the forward wants to leave, the club desires him off the wage bill, but can a suitor be found before 1 September? Oh and, Lisandro Martínez and Matthijs De Ligt, two frontline centre-backs, have only recently returned from injury.

Off-field picture

In early July United unveiled plans for their proposed new 100,000-seater stadium, located about 350 metres north-west of Old Trafford, insisting this is a “sanity, not vanity project”. Behind the catchy line, however, is a club in the red to the sum of £1.3bn. Omar Berrada, United’s chief executive, declared in March that £2bn was the working cost of the stadium, which is projected to be completed in 2035. This seems optimistic – try doubling it, maybe.

Owner-fan relationship

Untrusting, unhappy, annoyed, betrayed, toxic, broken, unmendable, etcetera: choose your pejorative when it comes to describing how most Manchester United fans feel about the Glazers. This has been the case regarding the six siblings, who are United’s majority owners, since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club in May 2013. Relations between fans and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s football department could also be rosier. Some are content due to last season’s third-place finish and the success of last summer’s buys – Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbuemo primarily. Others, though, are cheesed off about the current window’s business, the moving of season-ticket holders around the ground to free up seats for corporate packages, and the recent bid to eliminate touts that caused many genuine supporters to have to prove their innocence.

The manager

Like Ole Gunnar Solskjær before him, Carrick performed superbly in a caretaker capacity. The task now facing him is out-performing his former United team-mate and friend in the role of permanent manager, the Norwegian’s first full season in charge having ended in third place. Carrick’s prospects will be improved if by 1 September a left-back has been recruited. Given Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea and Tottenham have splashed far more cash than United on strengthening this summer, Carrick would no doubt take third – or any Champions League berth – if it was offered to him, albeit he is unlikely to admit as much.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s new midfield signing Youri Tielemans in action during a training session in Dublin. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

After being a major part of Aston Villa’s Europa League glory in May, and then captaining Belgium to the World Cup quarter-finals during the summer, Tielemans has been recruited to add drive, quality and a streetwisen touch to United’s midfield. His career shows a record of making the difference when required – he struck a memorable volley against Freiburg in Istanbul and powered in a long-range winner to claim the FA Cup for Leicester in 2021. There is no doubt about it – the son of Flemish Brabant is a big-game footballer.

Stat attack

Manchester United led the Premier League for shots last season, with 596. Much will depend upon Bruno Fernandes if they are to repeat this feat. He created at least 89 chances more than any other member of the squad and only fell six shy of taking the most shots. Fernandes turns 32 in early September; can he outrun age for another season?

Set for a breakthrough

Shea Lacey, the quick-footed diminutive winger from Liverpool, made four appearances under three different managers last season. On 21 December, an 84th-minute debut in the 2-1 loss at Aston Villa under Ruben Amorim made him academy product No 256 to feature for United. Eighteen days later, entering again on 84 minutes in the 2-2 draw at Burnley, Lacey’s next cameo was for Darren Fletcher. Fast-forward four days and Lacey lasted only 27 minutes of United’s 2-1 defeat to Brighton in the FA Cup after being sent off late on, later apologising. The 19-year-old had to wait five months before making his next appearance for United, this time under Carrick, entering in the 62nd minute of the final-day 3-0 victory at Brighton. He is now very much part of the first-team squad and one to watch.

World Cup impact

When England needed to stymie Argentina’s second-half onslaught in last month’s World Cup semi-final, with Anthony Gordon having put them 1-0 up, Thomas Tuchel became passive. Off went Gordon and Declan Rice and on came Ezri Konza and Nico O’Reilly. England subsequently crumpled, going on to lose 2-1. If Tuchel had instead turned to Kobbie Mainoo, a ball-carrying midfielder who could retain possession and move England up the field, Argentina may well have been thwarted. As it turned out, Mainoo did not play a second of the tournament. “I was in contact with him quite a bit through the summer [as] I’ve been in that position myself and not played at a World Cup,” Carrick said.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Arsenal have agreed a £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. The Premier League champions have been keen to find defensive cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber, who are out with injuries. They have tracked Konsa throughout the summer and have made a breakthrough in the negotiations.

Mikel Arteta hopes Konsa, whose Villa contract has two years to run, can make light of Saliba’s absence in central defence. The timeframe for the Frenchman’s return is unclear but he is not expected to play before mid-October, having sustained a back injury in France’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Spain. Konsa’s appeal is bolstered by the fact he can also play at right-back, where Timber is battling to return from a groin injury which has affected him for months.

Konsa starred for England on their run to the World Cup semi-finals. A fixture in Villa’s successful team, the 28-year-old will encounter fierce competition at Arsenal, especially when Saliba is fit. Arteta rates Saliba’s partnership with Gabriel Magalhães as the best in England but he thinks the addition of a player of Konsa’s calibre is a signal of Arsenal’s desire to build on their title success of last season and dominate.

The manager knows that his team played 63 matches in all competitions last season, which included runs to the Champions League and Carabao Cup finals, and he hopes to have a similar number this time out. As such, he believes he will be able to give Konsa the minutes he would expect, particularly when injuries are factored in. Arteta is also determined to have more high-quality options so that he can better rotate. At present, he has eight defenders, including Myles Lewis-Skelly, who can play in midfield.

Konsa joined Villa from Brentford in 2019 and has been central to their rise up the Premier League table under Unai Emery. He has made 286 appearances for them and was a part of the team that won the Europa League last season. Arsenal kick off the new season at home to Coventry on Friday night.

Meanwhile, Villa are braced for another bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins, after rejecting an offer worth almost £40m for the striker. Al-Hilal are pursuing a move for Villa’s all-time Premier League goalscorer, who has reached double figures in the top flight in his six seasons at the club after joining from Brentford.

If Villa sell Watkins, who has two years on his contract, they would seek to replace the 30-year-old England striker and Emery is a big admirer of Nicolas Jackson, but Chelsea’s valuation of £65m is thought to be prohibitive to any deal. There is an acceptance at Villa that any marquee arrival before the close of the window would probably have to follow another major sale, owing to the Premier League’s financial regulations.

Emery has had to significantly reshape his squad this summer after the departures of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, who joined Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, with Konsa now also on the move.

Villa have signed Zion Suzuki as a replacement for Emiliano Martínez, whose future remains unclear. Suzuki, a £30m buy from Parma, will be the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League.

Villa have completed the £17m signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atlético Madrid and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over a deal for João Palhinha and West Ham for Aaron Wan-Bissaka. Villa have also signed Johan Manzambi from Freiburg for a club-record £52m and João Gomes from Wolves for £38m. There could be further sales, with Villa hoping to find Martínez a new club.

Villa gave Watkins, together with Martínez and Konsa, an extended four-week break after the World Cup. Emery said Watkins volunteered to play in last week’s Super Cup against PSG, but the manager advised him to continue to rest.

Sports.title: Inter hold talks with Liverpool over deal for £30m-rated Curtis Jones
Sports.content:
Inter are in talks with Liverpool over a deal for Curtis Jones, with the 25-year-old expected to leave his boyhood club should the Italian champions offer around £30m. Jones has been a target for Inter since January and was the subject of a failed €25m bid from them in June.

Liverpool valued their homegrown midfielder closer to €40m, but with Jones in the final year of his contract, and no sign of an agreement over an extension, that figure is unlikely to be reached.

Intermediaries representing Inter contacted Liverpool in July with a proposal to pay up to €35m (£30m) for Jones. Negotiations between the clubs commenced on Wednesday. No agreement has been reached, but should Inter go to €35m as has been suggested, Liverpool are likely to sanction Jones’s departure. Inter’s willingness to pay Tottenham €35m for Djed Spence last week is seen as a benchmark figure for the Jones deal.

Jones, who has played six times for England, has been at Liverpool since the age of nine, but has been unable to secure a regular first-team starting role and cut a frustrated figure at times last season under Arne Slot.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Andoni Iraola, Slot’s replacement as head coach, spoke at his unveiling about the importance of keeping the Toxteth-born midfielder and of having a local identity in his team. But Inter’s determined pursuit and the risk of losing the player on a free transfer next summer have also to be factored in by Liverpool.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Sensible soccer: are football clubs actually signing the players they need?
Sports.content:
ROSEBUD

In the 1941 RKO Radio Pictures/Mercury repertory theatre production Citizen Kane, Orson Welles essayed a man who began as a whirlwind of prolific energy, only to spectacularly fizzle out, to the extent that near the end, stubborn pride his only remaining fuel, he could barely move around or achieve anything of note at all. Football Daily isn’t sure how any of this relates to Charles Foster’s namesake Harry, or his recent Geopolitics World Cup campaign; nor are we sure what bit of Welles’ career Harry’s mooted move from Bayern Munich to Al-Hilal would be comparable with. The flawed masterpiece The Magnificent Ambersons, perhaps, or that thing where he loses his mind over Findus peas.

But potential transfers are all the rage right now, nestled as we currently are in the otherwise barren taint betwixt the aforementioned GWC and the new domestic season. Arsenal are in the market for a centre-back, because they always are – the foundations built by George Graham go wide and deep – and are sniffing theatrically around Ezri Konsa of Aston Villa and Bayer Leverkusen’s Jarel Quansah. Either would suffice. Or possibly both. Quansah’s former club Liverpool are desperate for defensive reinforcements too, so naturally they’re concentrating their efforts on yet another slight forward, Ethan Nwaneri the latest name on a long list that also includes half of the PSG squad and will probably lead nowhere. To be fair, their sporting director Richard Hughes is reportedly off to Al-Hilal once this window shuts, and there’s all this Kane stuff going on, the poor man can’t be expected to do everything at once.

By way of contrast, Manchester United have been much more proactive in the market this summer. Having signed just a single useful central midfielder between 2007 and 2025 in Bruno Fernandes (subs please check), it now appears they’ll land three in as many months. They’ve already thrown Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans into that big gaping hole that’s been in the middle of Old Trafford for decades, and are now very close to adding 2024’s Carlos Baleba to the mix. The only question will be whether the difference between the £100m previously demanded by Brighton and the £65m the Cameroon international could now cost is either a smart bit of business by United or a big red flag. Football Daily certainly isn’t sure, so without anything useful to contribute, and the weather outside finally turning, we’re off to prepare for the onset of winter. Now, where’s that goddamn sled? We can never find that goddamn sled.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“We are so close to making history for unbeaten games in a row. This isn’t normal in football” – former Watford boss Xisco Muñoz tells Sam Cunningham how he plans to lead all-conquering Johor Darul Ta’zim to AFC Big Cup glory.

View image in fullscreen Xisco Muñoz has done a lot of celebrating this season. Photograph: Ashok Kumar/Getty Images

double quotation mark Don Revie and his merry henchmen [Tuesday’s Memory Lane, full email edition] getting ready for a night on the lash, as it was back then. Lest we forget: one-club man Jack Charlton once said ‘I cant play football, but I can stop those that can’. Diamond geezer eh?” – Alvin Jordan.

double quotation mark It was bewildering to read in Tuesdays’s Football Daily that ‘Kevin Lamour was a lone dissenting voice inside Fifa’s lair when Gianni Infantino’s plot to flog part of the World Cup to private investors – potentially on the cheap – was rumbled’. He was far from lone. Fifa’s secretary-general, Mattias Grafström, called the FFE plans a ‘sad and reproachable series of events’ in an email to staff. Fifa’s chief of global development, someone called Arsène Wenger, pronounced the withdrawal of FFE ‘absolutely necessary and beyond question’. Above all, Infantino’s right-hand man, the Fifa senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro, stated: ‘I cannot stand by while Fifa considers selling a stake in the World Cup. Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for Fifa’s member associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game.’ And unlike Lamour, Grafström, or Wenger, Cordeiro put his money where his mouth was and resigned” – Simon Skinner.

double quotation mark Talking of players’ wages, my Middlesborough friend who knew Wilf Mannion told me that when he was chosen to play for England at Wembley that they gave him a third-class rail ticket to get there. Unfortunately the train was so crowded that he had to sit on his suitcase in the corridor the whole way to London (not an unusual situation in those days)” – Bob Hopper.

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day winner is … Simon Skinner. Terms and conditions for our competitions can be viewed here.

Sports.title: Wafcon 2026 review: Glory for Cameroon, Nigeria flop and Malawi cause a stir
Sports.content:
Cameroon became only the fourth country to lift the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) title following Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea and South Africa, and only the third to have both a men’s and women’s continental champion, after a 3-0 win over Malawi in Rabat last weekend. The result was significant for several reasons, not least because it gave the competition a new winner after the former champions Nigeria and South Africa were eliminated in the quarter-finals to mark a changing of the guard in the African women’s game.

It is worth remembering that Cameroon did not directly qualify for this edition of the Wafcon and were only added when the tournament was expanded to 16 teams last November. That gave them the opportunity to compete, but almost no one would have picked them as champions based on reputation and results. Cameroon had not reached a Wafcon final in a decade and had never even scored a goal in the final, but had three before half-time against a Malawi side that seemed destined to complete a fairytale.

As debutants and the lowest-ranked team at the event in 153rd place, Malawi scorched their way into the final, in the process confirming a first World Cup appearance in Brazil next year. Malawi and Cameroon will be joined by Morocco and Algeria, who have qualified for the global event for the first time.

Wafcon winners and losers

Two months ago, the former Cameroon goalkeeper Valentine Nguele, who holds a Confederation of African Football (Caf) A coaching licence, was appointed as the national team’s first female coach. She came with a strong record after being part of the support staff at Louves Minproff that won the Cameroonian first division title five times between 2011 and 2020 and was also an assistant coach with FC Ebolowa, who won the title in 2024 and 2026. “Football is a true passion,” she said. “I love the moments I spend on the pitch every day. My style is participative and engaging.”

Under Nguele, Cameroon became a focused and clinical side, which they demonstrated by topping their group. In the quarter-finals they beat the 10-time champions Nigeria, then the hosts, Morocco, in the semi-final and, finally, Malawi. In the process Nguele became the fifth female coach to win Wafcon.

View image in fullscreen Valentine Nguele became the fifth female coach to win the Wafcon title. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPA

By contrast Nigeria failed to make the semi-finals for the first time. Worse was to come as they lost 2-1 to South Africa in their World Cup playoff, meaning they will be absent from the tournament for the first time. The Nigerian Football Federation subsequently sacked Justine Madugu and his entire technical team and announced plans to set up a taskforce to investigate the national team’s failure.

Another team who will be disappointed with their performance at Wafcon are Morocco, who participated in the previous two finals and would have hoped for third time lucky in front of their home fans. They were particularly poor in penalty shootouts, scoring once in four attempts against Cameroon in the semi-finals and twice in five against Algeria in the third-place playoff.

Stars of the tournament

The Cameroon goalkeeper Michaely Bihina won the competition’s golden glove for her ice-cold performances between the posts. Bihina’s standout showings came in the quarter-final, where she made nine saves against Nigeria. In the semi-final, she made three saves in regular time and three more in the penalty shootout to deny Morocco. Bihina kept a clean sheet in the final too, and conceded only two goals in six matches across the tournament.

Wafcon’s best player also came from Cameroon – the midfielder Monique Ngock, whose passion for football stems from watching the Indomitable Lionesses lose the 2016 final. Ngock was 12 years old at the time and remembered sobbing in disappointment. “When I cried in 2016, I said I will take my revenge one day if God gives me that opportunity. I will do everything to bring that trophy,” she said. Ngock very much fulfilled that vow by putting in several excellent performances in Morocco, including in the final, when she kept the dangerous Chawinga sisters in check.

View image in fullscreen Tournament star Monique Ngock of Cameroon reacts after the semi-final win against Morocco. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPA

Temwa Chawinga ultimately took the Golden Boot with five goals – the same number as Barbra Banda (Zambia), Inès Konan (Côte d’Ivoire) and Marie Ngah (Cameroon), who scored two in the final, but Chawinga also had two assists to her name.

Match of the tournament

Tanzania were responsible for the first upset of the tournament when they scored an 87th-minute winner to beat South Africa in the opening match of Group B. The following day Malawi pulled off a heist for the ages when they beat Nigeria 3-2. All the action came in the second half after Temwa Chawinga opened the scoring in the 73rd minute, her sister Tabitha doubling Malawi’s lead six minutes later. Nigeria responded from the spot in added time before Temwa struck again in the 95th minute to give Malawi a 3-1 lead. Nigeria threw everything at their opponents and scored in the 99th minute to set up a thrilling finale but Malawi held firm to begin a rollicking run to the final.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Most improved side

As bronze medallists, Algeria enjoyed their best Wafcon finish and also scored more goals at this tournament than in any previous edition – seven. They also had seven different goalscorers at the tournament, including the impressive 20-year-old Mélissa Bethi, who has been signed by Washington Spirit.

View image in fullscreen The hosts, Morocco, were well supported but other games were often sparsely attended. Photograph: Jalal Morchidi/EPA

Attendances

Stadiums were sparsely populated for most of the tournament, with on-the-ground reports indicating a lack of branding and awareness. Tickets went on sale less than a week before the tournament kicked off, priced between 20 and 50 Moroccan dirhams (£1.59 to £3.98), but such affordability did not have the required impact. This was also the third successive Wafcon held in Morocco, and though official numbers are not in they are unlikely to match the 2022 tournament, where more than 50,000 fans watched the final.

Get in touch

Sports.title: Not just big in Japan: Zion Suzuki has what it takes to follow Emiliano Martínez
Sports.content:
In November 2001, the first Japanese goalkeeper to play English league football conceded a goal within the first minute of his debut. Yoshikatsu Kawaguchi may have struggled for second-tier Portsmouth, conceding 21 times in his 12 league games after being spotted by the then director of football, Harry Redknapp, but he also produced some world-class saves and had glowing things to say about the Royal Mail.

Replaced by a 42-year-old Dave Beasant, Kawaguchi nevertheless remains a cult hero on the south coast, as a standing ovation in his final game demonstrated. Despite going on to play 116 times for Japan, he never made the jump to the Premier League. Now though, finally, Japan has a No 1 in the top flight.

Zion Suzuki has big gloves to fill at Aston Villa, where he is set to take over from Emiliano Martínez. In terms of mentality and self‑belief, succeeding a World Cup winner at a Champions League club will not be an issue. The 23-year‑old has already overcome plenty of barriers.

If much has changed in Japanese football in a quarter of a century, the same can be said of the past 30 months or so since the Asian Cup, when the US-born shot-stopper made a number of errors as Japan, the continent’s No 1 team, crashed out at the quarter-final stage. While some of his teammates did not exactly impress in Qatar, it was Suzuki who copped the blame.

That was tough enough to take for any goalkeeper, let alone a 20-year-old, but there was another level. The player with a Japanese mother and a Ghanaian-American father became the target of racist abuse online. “I’ve received [discriminatory comments] since elementary school, but I won’t give in to them,” Suzuki said. “I could have pretended to ignore [the messages], but I wanted to share my story in the hope that it could help not only soccer players, but athletes and young children with all kinds of roots.”

View image in fullscreen Zion Suzuki recovered from being targeted online after the Asia Cup to impress for Japan at this summer’s World Cup. Photograph: Jerome Miron/Imagn Images/Reuters

There are an increasing number of Japanese sports stars with mixed ethnic origin – tennis’s Naomi Osaka and the NBA’s Rui Hachimura, for example – and in football Suzuki is the highest‑profile. After a short spell with Urawa Reds, one of Japan’s and Asia’s biggest clubs, in August 2023 he left for a season in Belgium with Sint-Truiden. It went so well that, 12 months later, there was a five-year deal with Parma, where he quickly established himself.

One of the strongest goalkeepers around, his athleticism and shot‑stopping are not in doubt, as he showed during the World Cup, with a low save from Vinícius Júnior catching the eye. His positioning can still improve but he is good in the air (second in Serie A last season for crosses caught and high claims) and on the ground (second for successful long passes).

Adapting to England’s congested six-yard areas may take time and dominating the box like Martínez may take more. Since the Asian Cup, he has barely put a glove wrong for Japan and, despite a few mistakes at Parma, he was the main man between the sticks from when he joined until, well, Wednesday morning. Now, if Unai Emery can do what he does best then there is serious potential.

Suzuki can now help change the perception of Asian goalkeepers on a stage with a bigger global reach than Italy can offer. Attackers such as Son Heung-min and Kaoru Mitoma have lit up the Premier League and Abdukodir Khusanov has recovered from a dodgy start at Manchester City to become one of the league’s top defenders, but goalkeepers from Asia have not been common in England’s top flight.

There was Oman’s Ali al-Habsi, who played in the Premier League for Bolton and Wigan, impressing for the former against Bayern Munich in the Uefa Cup. Neil Etheridge of the Philippines played every game for Cardiff in 2018-19. Overall, though, it is slim pickings.

The World Cup did not help. At crucial times, Iraq, Uzbekistan and Jordan looked as if they could get results but then a goalkeeping error saw potential points lost. South Korean football has gone into meltdown since the World Cup, but had Kim Seung-gyu, usually a solid No 1, not dropped a clanger against Mexico then South Korea could have sealed a knockout stage spot with a game still to play and all the fallout may have been avoided.

While that is a lot to put on the powerful shoulders of the Samurai Blue stopper, he can make a difference. Despite being a trailblazer in Serie A, with Italian football still regarded, perhaps nostalgically in Asia, as the home of the strong defence and solid goalkeeper, his every move in Italy was not followed even back in Japan. This will be different. Success in the Premier League would not be a big deal just for Suzuki and Aston Villa.

Sports.title: ‘He doubted’: Mourinho says Real Madrid did not want Rodri after hesitation over move
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has confirmed Real Madrid made Rodri an offer and that he spoke to him about joining the club, but claimed the player’s doubts about the transfer made him unsure about signing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain.

On the same day Rodri was presented at Barcelona after the completion of a €75m (£65.4m) move from Manchester City that the midfielder said was “always my first choice”, Mourinho insisted he would not miss him at the Santiago Bernabéu. “I spoke to him a couple of times and Real Madrid made him a very good offer,” Mourinho said in an interview with El Chiringuito.

“Without negotiating with City, the club were in contact with Rodri and made him an important offer. Rodrigo had doubts, he doubted. And his doubts created doubts in me. He is an extraordinary player and he behaved in the right way with us. I have nothing bad to say. But Real Madrid are so big that you can’t have players who have to think twice. You get in touch with a player and the player says: ‘When do I go?’ That’s how it works.”

Rodri had three offers to leave City after the World Cup, from Paris Saint-Germain, Real and Barcelona. Having ruled out PSG because he wanted to return to Spain, the 30-year-old eventually chose Barcelona, where he will join eight of his teammates from the World Cup squad. When it was put to Mourinho that the move could be seen as a victory for Barcelona over their great rivals, he replied: “Victories are on the pitch, trophies.”

Real have not signed an alternative midfielder, despite their pursuit of Rodri and that being a clear hole in a team that have failed to win a major trophy in the past two seasons. Mourinho feels sure, however, that he does not need to bring in any further players. “I am not saying that there will not be any more signings because the market is still open, but if you ask me directly whether the squad is complete, for me yes it is,” said the 63-year-old at the start of his second stint managing the club. “It’s complete, closed. I like [my squad] a lot.

“I don’t miss Rodrigo. We have solutions, we have quality, we have players who maybe you look at and you judge them on what they have done but I like to think that I have the ability to improve players. A player that is one thing today can be a different player tomorrow.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa’s ideal Morgan Rogers replacement named amid Manchester United and Tottenham interest
Sports.content:
How does one go about replacing the most expensive British footballer in history?

Well, that's a problem Aston Villa boss Unai Emery must solve ahead of the 2026/27 campaign following Morgan Rogers' £117million exit to Chelsea earlier this summer.

4 Rogers helped end Villa's 30-year wait for a trophy Credit: Getty

The eye-watering nine-figure fee represents a significant profit on the initial £8m Villa forked out to sign Rogers from Middlesbrough in January 2024.

After a six-month period of adjustment, Rogers quickly cemented himself as one of Villa's most important players.

His brilliance in the final third was reflected by his 56 goal contributions across all competitions in the last two seasons, split evenly with 28 goals and 28 assists.

But Rogers' departure now leaves a gaping hole in Villa's line-up and it's one that won't be fixed on the cheap.

The reigning Europa League champions have already taken a step in the right direction by snapping up Johan Manzambi from Freiburg in a club record deal.

However, Manzambi's Villa debut may be some way away as he continues to recover from a knee injury sustained while representing Switzerland at the World Cup, with no definitive return date provided.

Andy Brassell reveals who Aston Villa should sign to fill Morgan Rogers void

While the 20-year-old recovers, Villa could still add extra strength to their attacking midfield stocks.

And according to European football expert Andy Brassell, Villa may find that in Como ace Martin Baturina.

"I think he makes a lot of sense for Aston Villa in a post-Morgan Rogers world," Brassell told talkSPORT.com.

"And he's a different player to Rogers of course. And you would expect Baturina ultimately to score more goals than him. So I feel that would work quite well.

4 Baturina has quickly become a talent to watch after his first season with Como Credit: Getty

"In terms of the blend that Manchester United are trying to put together. Yes I think he'd be a plus for them.

"But again, for me, Villa seems a really really good fit."

Is there another English team Martin Baturina could play for?

Another English team Brassell mentioned as a potential suitor for Baturina was Tottenham Hotspur.

However, Spurs already boast multiple players in Baturina's mould, which Brassell describes as 'more of a second striker' and 'someone who relies on excellent close control' in the box.

"And what they (Spurs) could do with is a big, brutish centre forward, essentially," Brassell continued.

"Look, I know De Zerbi wants to play fluid football. So maybe it does stack up. Maybe it could work.

4 Emery is in need of refreshing his attack following Rogers' move to Chelsea Credit: Getty

"But it wouldn't be my first choice destination for him."

How did Martin Baturina perform last season for Como?

Baturina, who joined Como from Dinamo Zagreb last summer, ended the 2025/26 campaign with eight goals and four assists across all competitions.

The 23-year-old boosted his transfer value with a goal during Croatia's 4-2 loss to England at the World Cup.

That can only be good news for Como, who are already one of Serie A's wealthiest clubs.

But that hasn't stopped club president Mirwan Suwarso from leaving the door open for a potential summer exit.

"If there's an offer, we'll listen," Suwarso told Calciomercato.

4 The 23-year-old helped Como qualify for the Champions League Credit: Getty

"If we like it, we'll accept it, but we're not afraid to refuse."

Why Martin Baturina will not be cheap for interested clubs

Suwarso's hard line stance is not ideal for Villa and other potential suitors, who almost certainly won't be able to strike a cut-price deal.

"There are two ways to look at it," Brassell told talkSPORT.com.

"Firstly, the fact is they're very well backed. A lot better backed than a lot of the traditional big names in Italian football. So to try and force them into a sale is quite difficult.

"As you said, if they're going to sell, they’ll sell on their terms.

"Baturina was really, really good last season. And bear in mind that as we spoke about before, that Alvaro Morata gap in terms of goals.

"They were short because he wasn't putting the ball in the back of the net. So they needed other people to chip in. Baturina was able to do that."

Sports.title: Man City urged to snub Enzo Fernandez and sign £60million Premier League alternative
Sports.content:
Manchester City have been told to consider signing Adam Wharton instead of Enzo Fernandez as they look to replace Rodri.

The Citizens are looking to add another midfielder to their ranks after influential midfielder Rodri left to join Barcelona for a fee in the region of £65million.



4 Rodri's departure to Barcelona has now been confirmed, after he previously looked set to join Real Madrid Credit: Getty

While the departure of Spain's World Cup-winning captain is a huge loss, City appear to have made replacing him a priority this summer.

Elliot Anderson was signed for £116m at the start of the window, and Morocco star Ayyoub Bouaddi is also expected to move to the Etihad, with personal terms agreed with Lille.

However, after Rodri's exit, another star is likely to be needed to bolster their midfield options.



Chelsea's Fernandez has been heavily linked with a move, although any deal is currently up in the air after the Citizens missed his 5pm deadline last Friday to complete their business.

Wharton tipped for big move

With Chelsea demanding £120m for Fernandez, City would once again have to complete a nine-digit transfer to snap up the Argentina star.



But talkSPORT's McCoist felt there is a better option available, and one which is likely to prove less expensive.

He pointed to Crystal Palace star Wharton, who has long been tipped for a big move, with Manchester United's interest already known.



Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, McCoist said: “I like him [Wharton] a lot…

"I think Wharton is more like Rodri than Fernandez is, I don’t think they’re going to get like-for-like now Rodri’s left, he’s the best at what he does.

“But I think you’d make a case that Wharton [is more like Rodri].

4 Wharton continues to be linked with England's biggest clubs Credit: Getty

4 Enzo Fernandez faces an uncertain future at Chelsea Credit: Getty



“The ball comes to him and the first thing he does is look forward, I really like him, I think he’d be an excellent signing.”

With Wharton earning huge praise for his ability to dictate play in midfield, this makes him more similar in profile to Rodri.

Palace’s price tag for him is unclear, although it was previously reported that Man United were plotting a £60m bid this summer.

That now appears unlikely to materialise, but if the Eagles demand a fee in this region, it would make Wharton a far cheaper option than Fernandez.



The 22-year-old has impressed since his move to Selhurst Park in February 2024, with his technical ability and vision catching the eye.

His exploits saw him named in England Euro 2024 squad, but he was a notable omission by Thomas Tuchel for this summer's World Cup.

4 A move to Man City would likely boost Wharton's England career, who has earned four senior caps to date Credit: Getty

Despite this, Wharton has continued to draw admirers, and his performance in Palace's Conference League final victory over Rayo Vallecano even saw him labelled good enough to play for Real Madrid or Bayern Munich.



The Blackburn academy graduate is poised to begin the new season at Palace, who are gearing up for Europa League football after Conference League glory.

There's also a new coach at the helm of Palace in Pierre Sage, who takes over from Oliver Glasner after he left at the end of his contract, but has since joined Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: National League South Club’s suspension extended with another fixture postponed
Sports.content:
National League South club Ebbsfleet United's suspension from the league has been extended by another match at least.

Concerns were raised about the club’s financial position and they had recently been subject to a winding up petition by HM Revenue and Customs [HMRC].



2 Ebbsfleet play in the National League South - but their opening three games are postponed Credit: Getty

The Fleet, who are managed by former Millwall, Leyton Orient and Gillingham player Josh Wright, were given a deadline 5pm on Tuesday, August 18 to provide satisfactory evidence that they can meet their financial obligations for the upcoming season.

After review from the National League’s Compliance and Licensing Committee on Wednesday, the suspension continues with another set for August 26.

As a result, Ebbsfleet will not be able to fulfil their fixture against AFC Totton on Saturday, having also not played their opening three fixtures against Slough Town, Folkestone Invicta and Chelmsford City have been postponed.



National League statement

A statement on Wednesday read: "The National League's Compliance and Licensing Committee convened this morning to further consider compliance by Ebbsfleet United FC with National League rules and regulations, and the suspension of the club in particular.

"The meeting was to consider the club's response. The Committee noted that debt to HMRC for PAYE arrears remained

outstanding and the winding up order was still in place.



"The Committee noted information provided to it around recent change in ownership of the club, and the financial position of the club, including the ability for the club under new ownership to meet the club's financial obligations for the 2026/27 season as required under rules and regulations.

"Following careful consideration, the Committee has taken the decision under applicable regulations to continue the suspension of Ebbsfleet United FC, with a further review of the position to be undertaken by the Committee on Wednesday 26 August, with a deadline for provision of information of 5pm on

Tuesday 25 August.



"As a result of continuation of the suspension, the Club will not be able to fulfil its home fixture on Saturday 22 August against AFC Totton.

"The Club remains subject to an embargo."

2 Ebbsfleet have also been under an embargo since July Credit: Getty

Ebbsfleet statement

Meanwhile, Ebbsfleet said on Wednesday: "The club has today at 16:26 received an update and response from the National League following today’s committee meeting.

"They have informed the club the submissions made yesterday do not satisfy the League committee’s requirements.



"They have requested more detail and clarification and extended the suspension for seven days.

"As a result, this Saturday’s originally scheduled fixture at home to AFC Totton has been postponed."

Kent-based Ebbsfleet were founded in 1946, originally as Gravsend and Northfleet, being elected to the Southern League, which is the seventh tier of English football.

Having spent years across non-league divisions, the club changed its name to Ebbsfleet in 2007.



Ebbsfleet has never been in the EFL having been relegated from the National League in the 2024/25 season.

Sports.title: Newcastle signing tipped to lose his starting XI spot within weeks of new season
Sports.content:
Newcastle signing tipped to lose his starting XI spot within weeks of new season

Lukas Hornicek may have been signed to become Newcastle's first-choice goalkeeper - but fans will shortly be begging for Nick Pope's return.

That's the view of England cricket icon and Magpies fan Steve Harmison, who believes the 24-year-old could lose his place in the team by October.

3 Hornicek is expected to be Newcastle's No.1 goalkeeper for the upcoming season Credit: AFP

Newcastle splashed out £25.7million to prise Hornicek away from Braga at the start of August.

Hornicek, who is regarded as one of Europe's top young shot-stoppers, has started three times for the Toon in pre-season.

But despite making a few glaring mistakes, he is expected to be named in Matthias Jaissle' starting XI in Sunday's Premier League opener against Liverpool at St James' Park.

The one-cap Czech Republic international is one of two goalkeepers that have joined Newcastle this summer along with Ewen Jaouen from Reims in a deal worth £18m.

It has been a summer of change in Tyneside so far this window, with the club selling Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon - while also releasing Kieran Trippier.

That is in addition to Eddie Howe stepping down, with Jaissle coming in to replace him in the dugout.

Newcastle have so far brought in six players - all aged 24 or younger - leading many to question whether they could challenge for a European spot.

What has been said about Newcastle's transfers this summer?

And when speaking on the talkSPORT Breakfast show on Wednesday, Harmison was asked whether Newcastle will struggle this season as a result of key players moving on.

To which said: "I just look at Newcastle's recruitment, I don't think they've improved the starting XI, which is an understatement because of what they've lost.

"I think some of the players that we have signed, I don't believe are quite ready to play in the Premier League.

3 Hornicek recorded 24 clean sheets across all competitions for Braga last campaign Credit: Getty

"[Sean] Steur looks a good player from Ajax, but he's 18, is he ready?

"Probably not to play against a [Alexis] McAllister or a [Dominik] Szoboszlai on the opening day of the season [against Liverpool]."

Will Nick Pope replace Lukas Hornicek in goal?

Moving on to the situation between the sticks, Harmison then tipped Pope to be recalled back to the line-up - despite many supporters wanting him sold.

The England international was even labelled as one of the Premier League's worst goalkeepers towards the end of last season.

Pope hasn't featured in pre-season since the 4-1 defeat at Bristol City last month.

Commenting on the No.1 battle, Harmison added: "I look at the goalkeeper, a lot of people talk about it.

3 Pope has featured in 131 games for the Magpies since joining from Burnley in 2022 Credit: Getty

"I'm going to make a statement, people won't like this from a Newcastle fans point of view.

"But I reckon we'll be calling for Nick Pope back in goal by October.

"Because Newcastle being under pressure, they might need somebody to keep the ball out of the net rather than a goalkeeper with good feet.

"I think they are little decisions the manager is going to have to take, because Newcastle, I don't think it'll be a bad, bad season.

"But I don't think it'll be a season of good cheer like we've had over the course of the first four-and-a-half-years from Eddie Howe."
