Sports.title: Liverpool told they spent Mohamed Salah’s wages on the wrong player
Sports.content:
Luis Diaz should have been the Liverpool player that was given a £400,000-a-week contract - not Mohamed Salah.

That's the bold view of ex-Reds midfielder Danny Murphy, who believes the Merseyside outfit have been made to regret selling Diaz.



3 Diaz was a fan favourite during his time at Anfield - winning five trophies Credit: Getty

The 29-year-old spent three-and-a-half-years at Anfield after joining from Porto in January 2022 for £45million.

But despite chipping in with 41 goals and 23 assists in 148 games across all competitions, the winger was sold to Bayern Munich last summer.

Having scored 17 times in the 2024/25 season - helping Liverpool win the Premier League title - he departed in a package deal worth £65.5m.



How much was Salah earning at Liverpool?

Diaz's exit came just three months after Salah penned a lucrative two-year contract extension worth a whopping £400k-per-week.

Less than 12 months later, the 34-year-old announced he would be leaving the club following the conclusion of the 2025/26 campaign on a free transfer.



Salah, who has linked up at Turkish side Trabzonspor, ultimately failed to live up to his previous heroics last term - scoring seven top-flight goals [12 in all competitions] - his lowest return since moving to Liverpool in 2017.

In contrast, Diaz enjoyed the best season of his career to date at the Allianz Arena - firing in 26 goals and supplying 23 assists to help Bayern win the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup.



And for Murphy, who won five trophies during his seven-year stay at Liverpool, he insists that Liverpool haven't been able to replace Diaz.

That is despite splashing out £446m on new signings last summer - a record-breaking figure from a single club in a window.

As well as parting ways with Diaz, Liverpool also sold Trent Alexander-Arnold, with fellow club icon Andy Robertson then released earlier this summer after having his minutes reduced for the following season.

3 Wingers Salah and Diaz helped spearhead Liverpool to the Premier League title in 2025 Credit: AFP



What has Danny Murphy said about Liverpool?

Speaking on the White and Jordan show on Wednesday, talkSPORT pundit Murphy commented on Liverpool's struggles last campaign, which saw them finish in fifth spot.

He said: "I think what happened with Liverpool at the beginning of last season [six defeats in opening 12 league game], they lost quality.

"Diaz... I know Salah's numbers were better, but I was one of the few that said, 'I'd rather Diaz stay and give him the money [from Salah's contract].'

"Because Salah was nearing the end, I know the year they won the league, he was a huge contributor [29 league goals].



"But Diaz was a big miss, [a] huge miss.

"And then Trent's gone, and for all the criticism of his defending, from an end product point of view, he was incredible, one of the best full-backs we've seen.

3 Diaz has established himself as one of the world's best forwards since making the move to Germany Credit: Getty

"Robbo [Robertson] got benched, completely unfairly, and actually [Milos] Kerkez struggled.

"So you started taking bits out, and what replaced them wasn't good enough.



"Then the [Alexander] Isak injury, it was a mixture of things.

"What [Andoni] Iraola has got to do in the first couple of months - especially as there's this need and expectation to be successful now and play good football with it.

"He's got to get the fans on board with what they're trying to do, I think he will."

The Iraola era at Liverpool begins against Newcastle at St James' Park on Sunday - a stadium the Reds haven't lost at since December 2015.

Sports.title: Championship club hit with winding up order and face disaster 12-point deduction and administration
Sports.content:
Championship club hit with winding up order and face disaster 12-point deduction and administration

Sheffield United could face administration and a 12-point deduction after the company its owners used to buy the club was given a winding up order.

The Blades were sold to current COH Sports Bidco for a fee of just over £100million in December 2024.



3 Sheffield United could be slapped with a possible points deduction Credit: Getty

But they could lose the Championship side if they do not hand over £35million they allegedly still owe United World, the investment arm of former owner of former owner Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud.

Failure to fork out the money could result in the Yorkshire outfit going into administration and being slapped with a whopping 12-point penalty deduction if the current co-owners Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen are declared insolvent.

United World argue that Eltoukhy and had effectively attempted to take the club without paying for it, after they transferred their shares in United to a new company.



The American pair dismissed the move as a 'publicity stunt' but the judge issued winding up order and the EFL are set to decide whether to take further action.

What have United World said?

United World insist it had made 'every effort to resolve the matter amicably' and tried to do so again on Wednesday morning 'to give the owners a final opportunity to spare Sheffield United the consequences of their actions.'



United World added: "It appears that Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen are simply not concerned about what this means for the club.

"What happens now is the result of their choices. United World will continue to pursue the full sums."



A Sheffield United spokesperson said: "Sheffield United Football Club is aware of today’s hearing at the High Court. This is a matter between the current owners and former owner.

"The football club is in contact with the EFL and the day-to-day operations at Sheffield United are unaffected."

And an EFL spokesperson added: "The EFL notes the High Court’s decision to issue a winding up order on COH Sports Bidco Limited.

"The League will consider the implications of that development in line with its Regulations, including whether any further action is required.



"In addition, the EFL continues to consider other regulatory matters following changes to the club’s ownership structure and developments within the wider group.

"As these issues remain ongoing, the EFL will make no further comment at this stage."

3 The EFL now must decide whether to take further action against the club Credit: Getty

Dispute between past and present Blades owners

United World said in a statement on Monday: "As the former owners of SUFC, United World does not want to see SUFC facing months of uncertainty that will follow the winding-up order being granted on 19 August.



"But in the absence of Eltoukhy and Rosen, both billionaires, agreeing to pay what they owe, we have no alternative but to take all legal steps to protect our interests.

"We understand that the EFL and the Independent Football Regulator (the IFR) are aware of this situation.

"But so far, we are not aware of any intervention by either.

"United World has issued this public statement in the hope that it is possible to avoid the potential consequences the club may face if this is not resolved before 19 August, after which we shall have no control over those consequences."

United commented on their disappointment in the statement made by Al Saud - insisting they are 'financially healthy'.



3 Sheffield United changed ownership in December 2024 Credit: Getty

Sources close to the current United ownership declared: "We are disappointed Prince Abdullah is trying to hurt the club and its supporters with publicity stunts.

"The deal between sophisticated parties in 2024 was well advised by his financial advisors.

"Sheffield United is financially healthy, unlike under Prince Abdullah when the club incurred a points deduction for missing payments to football creditors.



"Nonetheless, Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen invited Abdullah to re-invest in the Club and join the ownership of Sheffield United and to help use his skills to support our promotion efforts.

"Helmy and Steve are focused on the sustainability of the club and the season ahead."

United kicked off their Championship season with a goalless draw against Birmingham at Bramall Lane.

A 12-point penalty deduction would leave them 14 points off the play-off spots in the club's quest to seal a return to the Premier League.

Sports.title: Four new Match of the Day pundits announced as line-up released for 2026/27 season
Sports.content:
Four new Match of the Day pundits announced as line-up released for 2026/27 season

A new Match of the Day line-up has been announced ahead of the 2026/27 season.

Joe Hart, Steph Houghton, Danny Murphy, Micah Richards, Ellen White and Ashley Williams will continue to lend their insights, with Wayne Rooney and Alan Shearer returning to the studio.

2 Rooney and co will be back next season Credit: BBC

Match of the Day's new signings

Meanwhile, the BBC announced the addition of four new pundits.

Toby Alderweireld, Thomas Frank, Robbie Keane and Ashley Young have all joined the line-up for the 2026/27 campaign.

Former Tottenham and Brentford boss Frank was part of the broadcaster's team at this summer's World Cup.

Match of the Day will continue to be presented by Kelly Cates, Mark Chapman and Gabby Logan.

The trio took over hosting duties last season after the departure of long-time anchor Gary Lineker, who told talkSPORT in June he didn't miss doing the show.

Football fans were quick to notice a number of regulars, including Martin Keown and Dion Dublin, were not on the list.

Shay Given, Nedum Onuoha, Theo Walcott and Stephen Warnock were also omitted.

However, talkSPORT understands contract negotiations are ongoing and all are expected to be used across the BBC's coverage this upcoming season.

Match of the Day here to stay

In 2023, the BBC agreed a deal to continue showing free-to-air Premier League highlights on Match of the Day until the 2028/29 campaign.

Commenting on the broadcaster's offering for the upcoming season, BBC director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski said: "Football means something different to every fan, and this season BBC Sport is putting those fans even more firmly at the heart of the game.

2 Ashley Young is joining Match of the Day after retiring from playing earlier this year Credit: Getty

"We're bringing together the unrivalled expertise of former players and managers with the passion, personality and perspectives of supporters to create a richer football experience wherever and however audiences follow the game."

The first edition of Match of the Day in 2026/27 will air on Saturday at 10:20pm on BBC One, featuring the best of the action from the start of the new Premier League campaign.

And the action all gets underway on Friday night, with reigning champions Arsenal welcoming newly promoted Coventry City to the Emirates Stadium, live on talkSPORT.

The remaining nine opening fixtures take place across Saturday, Sunday and Monday.

Sports.title: New Premier League rule to mean English football has completely new look this season
Sports.content:
New Premier League rule to mean English football has completely new look this season

Premier League shirts will carry a whole different look for the first time in over two decades this season.

The front-of-shirt ban on gambling sponsors in England's top-flight is effective from 2026/27, that is affected nearly half of the teams.

3 Forest played in pre-season without a front-of-shirt sponsor Credit: Getty

Eight clubs were forced to ditch gambling companies' logos that were emblazoned on their shirts last campaign.

The voluntary ban was passed by Premier League clubs in April 2023, but the sponsor shake-up has taken until the summer to take hold.

Fulham opened up the floodgates for betting firms to adorn the front of Premier League shirts in the 2002/03 season.

However, over 20 years later, the new rules have seen several teams scrambling to secure new sponsors on the eve of a new campaign.

Which teams are still without a front-of-shirt sponsor?

Nottingham Forest played in pre-season without a front-of-shirt sponsor after removing the Bally’s logo that appeared last year.

Oliver Glasner's men have now agreed a deal with Global financial services platform Marex, but Chelsea are still without a main sponsor.

The Blues believe the value remains around £50million, and with no partner as of yet willing to meet that, they will enter another season with an empty space in the middle of their kits.

talkSPORT host and Chelsea fan Andy Jacobs claimed: "Surely getting £20m a year is better than nothing. And because they wanted 40 or 50 and each year they don't get it, they're losing that money!"

Asked about the economics of such a stance, Football Finance Expert Kieran Maguire referenced the increase in sponsored training kits and shirt sleeves.

3 Chelsea have struggled to find a sponsor to meet their valuation in recent seasons Credit: Getty

He told Hawksbee & Jacobs: "I think there is an issue in terms of the front of the shirt because we've got the start of the voluntary ban coming in this season, which prohibits gambling sponsors.

"But I believe Forest have signed up with a sponsor in the last 90 minutes or so. So it only leaves Chelsea and Sunderland."

Crystal Palace and Fulham have switched from gambling to technology and AI, to join Ipswich and Manchester United in the tech sponsorship industry this season.

Man United exploit Premier League loophole

The Red Devils have already announced a multi-year sponsorship deal worth £20m per season with Betway to sponsor their training kit.

Maguire added: "What has happened as a result of the ban on gambling on the front of shirt, we've seen the value of shirt sleeve deals go up, and we've seen the value of training deals go up.

3 United have confirmed their new sponsorship deal with Betway ahead of the 2026/27 season Credit: Getty

"And Manchester United have got a very spectacular one, which they signed off with again in the last few weeks.

"So there still is money to be made.

"Chelsea are adamant that they're not going to sell the club cheap, and they're looking for a long-term partner.

That has not been matched by the willingness of other parties to sign a long-term deal. So that's why we've got this bit of a standoff at present.

"They could have signed a £20m pound one-year deal.

"It's Chelsea, they're a global brand, they're regularly playing in the Champions League, they played in the Club World Cup and so on.

"All of these things should have been a positive. And it does make you scratch your head as to why they've effectively just thrown money down the drain."

Sports.title: Chelsea launch new outcast training group of stars working separately to team-mates ahead of potential exits - as Blues look to trim squad
Sports.content:
Chelsea launch new outcast training group of stars working separately to team-mates ahead of potential exits - as Blues look to trim squad



See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have created a second training group who are working separately to Xabi Alonso’s main squad, including Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson ahead of their potential departures.

Both Delap and Jackson could yet leave this summer either permanently or temporarily, while Mykhailo Mudryk has also participated in these alternative sessions with the 25-year-old Ukrainian available for a loan after his suspension from football for anti-doping offences ended.

Chelsea have attempted to get away from the ‘bomb squad’ accusations which have plagued the Premier League club in past years.

This time, they are allowing this second group to work at the same time and on the same training pitch and use the same first-team facilities.

Raheem Sterling was previously among those who had to work on his own at their Cobham headquarters.

Chelsea sources have described it as a fluid group with players coming and going, depending on workloads and what Alonso wants in his main session, and deny any suggestion that only those up for sale or loan have been training separately.

Chelsea have created a second training group that is working separately to Xabi Alonso’s main squad

The group includes several stars who may depart like Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson (left)

Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson have been involved in these other sessions as they get up to speed, for example, along with younger players.

After loaning Reggie Walsh to League One Wigan on Wednesday, Chelsea’s website now lists 41 player profiles for their senior squad.

That does not include Axel Disasi, who has also been working separately from Alonso’s sessions while he works on securing his exit.

Tosin Adarabioyo, who has interest from England and Europe, is also believed to have been with this second group.

Enzo Fernandez, Malo Gusto and Pedro Neto, who have all been linked with leaving and valued at £120million, £75m and close to £100m respectively, have been training with Alonso’s main group.

Chelsea are working on slimming their bloated squad before their 2026-27 season officially starts, with Alonso’s first Premier League fixture in charge coming away at Fulham this Monday.

Sports.title: Everton ponder Cash grab from Aston Villa... who are braced for fourth Ollie Watkins bid from Saudi side - as Newcastle are offered former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Reijnders seals Saudi move Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has joined Al Qadsiah for £52m. Reijnders will work under Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah. The 28-year-old, who has an offer from Nottingham Forest also, only joined City from AC Milan last summer for £46.3m and made 50 appearances, scoring seven goals. Tijjani Reijnders is leaving Manchester City after just one season Clarets land Coudet Burnley have signed goalkeeper Gregoire Coudet from French side Brest on a permanent deal. The 27-year-old has signed a four-year contract. Norwich City have signed Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan. The Championship club will pay a proportion of the 25-year-old's salary after finding a replacement for Ali Ahmed following his knee injury. Inter hopeful of £30m deal for Jones Liverpool and Inter Milan have resumed talks over a deal for Curtis Jones today, initiated by the Italian side. There is currently no agreement for the 25-year-old but terms are being discussed. Something in line with the package and structure Inter utilised to sign Tottenham defender Djed Spence - €35m (£30m) - will likely see a deal agreed for the midfielder between the clubs. However, club sources underline these are verbal negotiations at present, and no actual agreement has been reached. Toffees consider Cash grab Everton are showing interest in Aston Villa right back Matty Cash as they assess all options in the market. Villa are signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham today and he is being brought in to increase competition for Cash in the right-back berth. Poland international Cash has three years left on contract. Everton have been working through a raft of names to try and solve their issue at right-back which has even prompted questions from Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Barca keep tabs on Kane Barcelona are monitoring Harry Kane's contract talks with Bayern Munich. The England captain is giving priority to resolving his future with the German champions where he is settled and discussions are ongoing about the length of deal for the 33-year-old. Kane is understood to want a three year deal and, as Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this summer, Barca have made their interest known. Read the full story here. Villa braced for another Watkins bid Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old. Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki. Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma. Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa. The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays. As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today. The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million. There's a new Cherif in town Coventry have completed their ninth signing of the summer transfer window with Fenerbahce striker Sidiki Cherif for £20.5million. The deal has taken the club's spending to over £120m. The 19-year-old, who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January, made appearances in the Europa League and in this season’s Champions League qualifiers prior to opening talks with Coventry. Toon's Nkunku offer Newcastle have been offered the chance to sign former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku from AC Milan. However, their priority remains to sign a midfielder first hence talks with Man City for Nico Gonzalez. Other targets are also being discussed. Nkunku has been told he can leave Milan and has interest from RB Leipzig among others. ... and they're closing in on Diabate Newcastle are also closing on Genclerbirligi’s midfielder Ousmane Diabate. The highly-rated 18-year-old had been set for Brentford while Tottenham had also shown interest. However, Newcastle look to have won the race with the teenager likely to stay on loan in Turkey for another season. Diabate, a defensive midfielder, has played 10 matches for the U19s and seven for Genclerbirligi’s first team so far. Liverpool defensive prospect in talks over La Liga move Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is in talks to join Levante on loan. The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England so is having to be loaned out. The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future. First team football in a top league such as La Liga is viewed as an integral next step. He also has interest from Portugal and Germany. Winger Kieran Morrison is joining Sheffield Wednesday on loan today. Liverpool continue to discuss a move for Bradley Barcola at Paris St Germain but a deal for his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye is unlikely. Konsa nearing Arsenal move... Arsenal have agreed a £51million deal plus add-ons for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa. The England international has said goodbyes to staff at Villa and is due to undergo a medical tomorrow. Read the full story here. As Gunners move for United youngster Arsenal are also working on a deal for 20-year-old right back Habeeb Ogunneye from Manchester United. Arsenal want players to boost their U21s squad and have also shown interest in United's James Scanlon. Gibraltar international winger Scanlon was on loan at Swindon Town last season. England youth international Ogunneye had a spell at Newport on loan. Baleba close to United switch Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba. Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared. Read the full story here. Pogba tears up Monaco deal Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end. The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS. Read the full story here. Paul Pogba's time at Monaco is over - with MLS clubs now considering a move for the former Man United midfielder Farke reunites with Elvedi Leeds have signed Nico Elvedi from Borussia Monchengladbach. The final fee is £6.5m rising to £8.5m with bonuses. The 29-year-old Switzerland international centre back worked with Daniel Farke previously at the Bundesliga club. James set for Wolves move Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical. The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m. He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham. Chelsea defender closes on Italy move Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning. The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m. Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal. The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains. The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull. Piroe party at West Ham West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season. The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League. Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons. Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League. 'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.' Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League. The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy. Potters snare Ipswich pair Stoke have agreed a fee of around £6million with Ipswich for striker George Hirst and are also taking Ipswich full back Ben Johnson on loan. Scotland international Hirst is to undergo medical later today. The fee will increase on performance related bonuses. Sports.title: Referees chief Howard Webb slams FIFA over Folarin Balogun red card scandal
Sports.content:
Refs' boss Howard Webb has piled into FIFA over the World Cup scandal of Folarin Balogun’s suspended red-card ban.

England’s head of officiating said he was ‘really troubled’ by the saga, which marred the summer’s showpiece.

US striker Balogun was shown a red card in the co-host’s round of 32 victory over Bosnia, which triggered an automatic one-match ban.

However, after the extraordinary and unprecedented intervention of US president Donald Trump, FIFA decided to suspend the ban for 12 months, meaning he was free to play in the last-16 fixture with Belgium.

The saga prompted claims of corruption, with the integrity of the global competition significantly undermined.

‘I was really troubled by it,’ Webb said. ‘We know that there was pressure placed by a politician onto FIFA because that was admitted, and we know that the suspension was taken away for that particular tournament and suspended through a process which seemingly didn't exist before the season the tournament started.’

Donald Trump called FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to ask him to review Folarin Balogun's sending off at the World Cup

The striker was sent off for this challenge during their 2-0 win over Bosnia but his suspension was overturned

Speaking ahead of the new season, Webb added that the move could now spark unfair conspiracy theories across the game.

‘Where I was troubled by it was that we live in a world now which is different to the one that I occupied as a ref, in that decisions that are taken previously were viewed as correct or incorrect,’ he explained.

‘Far too often now, decisions are viewed as correct or corrupt by people who want to type all over social media. They try to draw inferences around decisions around decisions, but they don't agree with them. What's the motivation behind that decision?

‘When you get that type of situation, it opens up space for people to think, “Ha ha! You see, this sort of thing's happening all the time behind the scenes”, and it's really not, in my experience.’

Webb’s comments were echoed by Premier League boss Richard Masters. ‘We should be looking back on the World Cup and the football that was played, and Spain being obviously the best team, and England’s agonising semi-final defeat,’ he said.

‘But we’re not, we are talking about other issues, and I think that’s a huge shame. The Balogun issue stands alone in that isolated incident which is very difficult to comprehend when you look at it. I think it is, again, a self-inflicted moment.’

Meanwhile, Webb said that Pro Ref had increased support to referees following the situation with disgraced former official David Coote, who was given a suspended jail sentence after pleading guilty to making an indecent image of a child.

They have brought in a head of performance psychology, along with a robust reporting process in which any concerns can be raised.

Sports.title: Championship club Sheffield United at risk of 12-point deduction - with owners' company hit by winding-up order - as EFL investigate damaging breaches of rules
Sports.content:
Sheffield United are in danger of a 12-point deduction after the company its owners used to buy the club was hit with a winding up order.

Blades fans will now face an anxious wait, with the EFL investigating whether there has been a potentially damaging breach of its rules.

United World, the investment arm of former owner Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, took COH Sports Bidco to the High Court, claiming it was owed £35m from the sale, which took place in 2024.

It argued that current custodians of the Championship side, American duo Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen, had effectively attempted to take the club without paying for it, after they transferred their shares in United to a new company.

While the Americans dismissed the move as a ‘publicity stunt’, a judge issued the winding up order and the EFL will now decide whether to take further action.

Sheffield United face a nervous wait to see if they are handed a points deduction

A United World spokesperson said it had ‘made every effort to resolve the matter amicably’ and had tried to do so again this morning ‘to give the owners a final opportunity to spare Sheffield United the consequences of their actions’.

‘It appears that Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen are simply not concerned about what this means for the club,’ it added.

‘What happens now is the result of their choices. United World will continue to pursue the full sums.’

A Sheffield United spokesperson said: 'Sheffield United Football Club is aware of today’s hearing at the High Court. This is a matter between the current owners and former owner.

'The Football Club is in contact with the EFL and the day-to-day operations at Sheffield United are unaffected.'

An EFL spokesperson, meanwhile, added: ‘The EFL notes the High Court’s decision to issue a winding up order on COH Sports Bidco Limited. The League will consider the implications of that development in line with its Regulations, including whether any further action is required.

‘In addition, the EFL continues to consider other regulatory matters following changes to the club’s ownership structure and developments within the wider group. As these issues remain ongoing, the EFL will make no further comment at this stage.’

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential transfer special: The target sources insist is 'all in' on Reds move, update on Ibrahim Mbaye and the young midfielders who have won over Andoni Iraola, revealed by LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Liverpool still have a huge to-do list in the transfer market if they are to lay the foundations for a successful season.

The window closes at 11pm on Tuesday, September 1, which means there is now less than a fortnight for the Reds to do, well, a lot of business.

Top of the shopping list is a wide forward to replace Mohamed Salah, while they could also recruit a second winger.

Liverpool have had a quiet summer so far, with the only additions £34.5million winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna, and defender Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona for the season.

Jeremy Jacquet did, however, arrive this summer after his £60m move from Rennes was agreed in January. For what it is worth, the finances of that deal will count on this year’s accounts, taking their summer spend to just north of £100m.

But what else is left to do? Daily Mail Sport's Merseyside expert Lewis Steele answers the big questions...

Andoni Iraola's squad could still do with plenty of additions with just a few weeks to go in the transfer window

The Reds look particularly light on the wing, despite the £35million signing of Victor Munoz from Osasuna

What's going on with the winger pursuit?

Bradley Barcola is desperate to join Liverpool, according to sources. The Paris Saint-Germain and France forward is said to be ‘all in’ on making this move happen.

He has been the top target for some time, going back to when RB Leipzig turned down an £86m approach for winger Yan Diomande, who has since joined Real Madrid for roughly £120m.

PSG have been stubborn over their valuation of Barcola, though. The French and European champions value him at around £145m, which Liverpool view as too high.

PSG have forwards aplenty, having signed Mika Godts from Ajax, World Cup hero Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco.

Akliouche, while we are on the topic, is another Liverpool had a look at earlier in the summer but it was always clear the young Frenchman fancied a move to Paris.

These incomings could see PSG soften their valuation of Barcola, with Liverpool also previously on the tail of 18-year-old team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye.

Bradley Barcola (left) is desperate to join Liverpool and has been the top target for some time

So, could they sign both Barcola AND Mbaye?

The Barcola chase is straightforward. Liverpool want him, he wants Liverpool, PSG will do a deal if the price is right.

Mbaye, however, is less clear-cut – and there are two sides to the story.

Reports in French newspapers suggested on Tuesday that he has an agreement to join Liverpool. This has been played down by sources in England, who insist that interest was merely exploratory.

The signings of Munoz and Araujo accelerated quickly, so perhaps that could happen again. For example, Liverpool first made contact with Araujo’s camp four days before he flew to England for his medical.

What we do know is that Liverpool will likely begin the season with wing options of Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Munoz, with the out-of-favour Federico Chiesa and young Lewis Koumas lurking in the background.

Two more wingers, especially with Gakpo subject to interest from Tottenham, would certainly be welcome. Maybe the dominoes will soon start to fall…

Reporting in France and sources in England differ in their view of Liverpool's pursuit of Ibrahim Mbaye (right)

Will Liverpool sign a midfielder?

Curtis Jones is on the verge of joining Inter for around £30m after a summer-long back and forth.

The England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

The Italian champions had a bid of around £21m turned down earlier in the summer and, if they sign Jones, he will be the third Englishman they have bought this window after John Stones and Djed Spence.

Will they sign a midfielder to replace Jones? As it stands, no – though that could change if a deal becomes available in the last week of the market.

Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton has long been linked with a move but the Selhurst Park club would want a huge fee of around £100m – and there is no indication Liverpool are interested anyway.

Many other midfielders have been mooted but it seems more likely than not that the Reds do not sign a midfielder this window.

That would mean two youngsters will be promoted. Trey Nyoni, who excelled in pre-season and was perhaps Liverpool’s stand-out player on the American tour, is pushing for more minutes and looks more than capable. The 19-year-old has also had plenty of interest.

It is understood James McConnell’s loan move to Championship side Preston has been kiboshed – for now at least – by Liverpool in the last days despite regular game-time being promised.

North End had a deal agreed and met the player but Liverpool pulled the plug.

James McConnell's proposed loan to Preston was cancelled by Liverpool, with McConnell having impressed Iraola

The young midfielder, who spent time at Ajax last season, knocked on the door of boss Andoni Iraola last Friday and was told he is part of his plans after impressing in training and there will be minutes for him in the first team this year.

McConnell also had a meeting with sporting director Richard Hughes, who stressed there is no official pecking order in the midfield so both Nyoni and McConnell can push for minutes.

Will they recoup any money?

Alexis Mac Allister was linked with Real Madrid but nothing was forthcoming and his father, Carlos, has publicly denied any talks with other clubs. Mac Allister has two years remaining on his deal and no new contract is on the table.

The sale of Jones represents a good cash injection, especially for a player with just one year remaining on his deal.

There is also the Gakpo conundrum, with Spurs sniffing around.

Harvey Elliott has failed to take his chance in pre-season after returning from a year to forget at Aston Villa. Some of that might be to do with the fact he has barely played in the last 12 months and his fitness level is not where it should be.

Chiesa started the US tour well with a goal against Sunderland. Speaking after that, he said he was committed to the club and wanted to prove people wrong. But there are a few clubs monitoring his situation and, as ever, Chiesa’s future looks uncertain.

Federico Chiesa has long been out of favour at Liverpool and his future is uncertain

Any other loans?

Young defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is on the verge of joining La Liga outfit Levante on a season-long loan.

The 18-year-old has been a revelation in pre-season, playing regularly at the heart of defence and winning praise from Iraola.

But Ndukwe does not have a work permit due to a complex new set of regulations. He signed from Austria Vienna in January.

Levante are set to win the race ahead of multiple other clubs across Europe. Liverpool will review the loan in January, by which point he should have the required points to play in England.

Kieran Morrison is on the verge of a loan to Sheffield Wednesday, who are racing to get the winger registered in time to make their squad to face Bradford on Thursday night.

Koumas has a queue of clubs wanting to take him on loan. But his future is less clear-cut as, like McConnell, Iraola has taken a shine to him in pre-season and he could be asked to stick around.

Defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is set to move on loan to Levante and is a player to keep an eye on

The former Hull, Birmingham and Stoke loanee, son of former Premier League midfielder Jason, could see his situation change if Liverpool were to be busy in terms of incomings.

Defender Luke Chambers also has suitors but it is believed he will not go on loan for the sake of it. Iraola likes the 22-year-old, who excelled on loan at Charlton last season and can play centre half and left back.

Calvin Ramsay is another on the list of potential exits, with St Mirren tracking him, though fellow full back Owen Beck is set to stay after a setback in his recovery from injury.

Sports.title: Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as he reveals his secret ban and will 'step away from public life to get myself right'
Sports.content:
Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as he reveals his secret ban and will 'step away from public life to get myself right'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios has been banned from tennis after testing positive for cocaine.

The 31-year-old submitted a sample while playing in Mallorca on June 22 that contained benzoylecgonine, a substance found in the class A drug.

Kyrgios said he took ‘full responsibility’ for his mistake and was ‘deeply disappointed’ in himself.

The Australian has been suspended since August 4, meaning he cannot play in, coach at, or attend any professional men’s or women’s tournament, including Grand Slams such as Wimbledon.

Kyrgios can appeal against the provisional ban, which could see him face between three months and four years on the sidelines.

His ban could also be reduced if he can prove that he did not take the substance for performance-enhancing benefits.

The Australian was the runner-up at Wimbledon in 2022 – his only Grand Slam final to date – losing to Novak Djokovic but won the men's doubles at the Australian Open in the same year.

He has battled knee and wrist injuries in recent years that have seen him make limited appearances at major tournaments.

Kyrgios, who was once the 13th highest-ranked player in the world, announced his suspension in a lengthy statement on Instagram today.

The post read: 'I wanted you to hear it from me first. I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine.

'I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.

'I am sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors, and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.

'I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

Former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios has been banned from tennis after testing positive for cocaine

The former world No 13 in Brisbane, Australia, in January... he has endured a series of disappointing seasons due to injuries

'I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone.

'None of that excuses what I did.

'However, the good news is that this has given me a wake-up call. For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

'I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family.

'I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better. Nick.'

Kyrgios played in Majorca at the Association of Tennis Professionals 250 event in late June, losing his singles match to fellow Australian Adam Walton in straight sets on June 22.

He later withdrew from the doubles, where he and partner John-Patrick Smith had been due to play Austin Krajicek and Nikola Mektic the following day.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), the sport's anti-doping body, has since announced that Kyrgios has been handed a mandatory provisional suspension.

A statement read: 'The International Tennis Integrity Agency has provisionally suspended Australian tennis player Nick Kyrgios under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme.

'Kyrgios provided a sample during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca, Spain, on June 22, 2026. On July 17, 2026, a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory confirmed the presence of benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

'Cocaine is a stimulant and substance of abuse on the WADA Prohibited List and is banned in competition under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme. If taken out of competition, reduced sanctions apply for substances of abuse.

Kyrgios was the runner-up at Wimbledon in 2022 - his only Grand Slam final to date - losing to Novak Djokovic

'Because of the nature of the substance, a provisional suspension is mandatory and has been in place since August 4, 2026.

'Kyrgios, who reached a career-high world singles ranking of 13 in October 2016, has the right to appeal the provisional suspension, but has not done so to date.

'As with all Tennis Anti-Doping Programme cases, ITIA support is available to Kyrgios.

'While suspended, Kyrgios is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.'

Before his suspension, Kyrgios's appearances on the professional tour had been limited, with the Australian star only taking part in a clutch of events due to his ranking of 919.

He has not won a singles match since last year's Miami Open but has been offered wildcard entries at both singles and doubles events.

Former British star Dan Evans was handed a one-year ban in 2017 after testing positive for cocaine at the Barcelona Open.

The drug had been found in the pocked of his washbag but the International Tennis Federation accepted his explanation that he had been contaminated after the drug found its way onto his finger or medication in the bag accidentally.

Kyrgios's case represents the second high-profile anti-doping revelation in tennis in recent months, after 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova was handed a four-year ban in June for refusing to take a drugs test.

Sports.title: Barcelona keep close eye on Harry Kane contract talks with Bayern Munich - with the England captain seeking a three-year deal to stay in Germany
Sports.content:
Barcelona keep close eye on Harry Kane contract talks with Bayern Munich - with the England captain seeking a three-year deal to stay in Germany

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Barcelona are monitoring Harry Kane's contract talks with Bayern Munich.

The England captain is giving priority to resolving his future with the German champions where he is settled and discussions are ongoing about the length of deal for the 33-year-old.

Kane is understood to want a three-year deal and, as Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this summer, Barca have made their interest known.

Al Hilal are also keen on Kane even though they are pursuing Aston Villa's Ollie Watkins too.

Kane has entered the final 12 months of the four-year deal he signed with Bayern after his £86.4m move from Tottenham in 2023.

He scored 61 goals in 51 appearances in all competitions for Bayern last season as Vincent Kompany's side completed a league and cup double, and said: 'We obviously said we wanted to talk after the World Cup and after my holiday. So I'm not sure exactly when, but they'll start this week, next week... we'll start those talks.

Harry Kane has entered the final 12 months of his deal at Bayern Munich and Barcelona are monitoringthe striker

'Like I've said before, we're calm, I think they're calm with the situation.

'Obviously now is the time to start talking, because there's only a year left. That's important. But both sides are relaxed, and I'm pretty sure there'll be some talks this week or next week.'

Barcelona are exploring options in the market as Atletico Madrid cling on to their number one target Julian Alvarez.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree £51m deal for Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa as Gunners bolster their defensive ranks
Sports.content:
Arsenal have agreed a £51million deal plus add-ons for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa. The England international has said goodbyes to staff at Villa and is due to undergo a medical tomorrow. Arsenal have been looking for a new defender with William Saliba out for months after injuring his back and Jurrien Timber also sidelined with a long-term groin problem. The fee is a triumph for Villa as Arsenal initially valued the 28-year-old, who had two years remaining on his contract, at £30m. He was not part of Unai Emery's squad for the UEFA Super Cup defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week as he was away on holiday after the World Cup. Konsa featured 48 times last term in all competitions, scoring two goals and contributing one assist, as Unai Emery's side lifted the Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League to secure Champions League football for 2026-27. He also sported the armband in John McGinn's absence as Villa's vice captain. Arsenal and Aston Villa are closing on agreement for England international Ezri Konsa

Konsa played in every game of England's World Cup run as the country finished third. Konsa started seven of the Three Lions' eight matches at the tournament, with Thomas Tuchel largely partnering him with Marc Guehi at the heart of the defence. Sports.content:
1.50 Sky Bet Lowther Stakes - WILD BLOSSOM looks ready for the step up to six furlongs - and the return to Group company.

Racing's 300,000-guinea breeze-up purchase could hardly have got her career off to a better start than when running away with a novice stakes for fillies at Carlisle in May by 10 lengths from subsequent Listed winner Crownbreaker.

Given her trainer Karl Burke’s depth of two-year-old talent, it was no surprise to see the daughter of sent off at just 7-1 for the Group 2 Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot next time. But a draw in stall seven did for Wild Blossom’s chances and, under the circumstances, a 10th-of-27 finish, just over four lengths behind winner Victorious, could have been a lot worse.

Plus, grab a £2 free shop bet inside Thursday and Friday's paper too! And that's not all - get a packed racing pullout from the expert team you trust every day of the iconic York meet from Wednesday 19 until Saturday 22 August 2026. Find out more here.

‌



Burke then sent James Doyle’s partner to Glorious Goodwood for the Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes and the retrieval mission went to plan as Wild Blossom got back to winning ways with a length-and-a-half defeat of Fast Track.

Although she has raced exclusively at the minimum trip, my selection shouldn’t be troubled by tackling an easy six today and has the untapped potential to make an impression at Group 2 level. Libertango , winner of Royal Ascot’s Group 3 Albany Stakes, is likely to have a say in proceedings, while Star Of State and In The Black are others who merit a second look.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 WILD BLOSSOM, 2 LIBERTANGO, 3 IN THE BLACK

View 7 Images Sun Goddess: Newsboy's tip (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

‌



2.25 Harry's Half Million By Goffs - SUN GODDESS, as a Group 1 winner, is emphatically the clubhouse leader.

Having come home strongly on her debut to force a dead-heat for second behind Aidan O’Brien stablemate Carry The Flag at Naas in May, Sioux Nation’s daughter duly went one better with a five-length supremacy at the Curragh 15 days later.

Sun Goddess went off the 10-11 favourite for the Group 3 Albany Stakes at Royal Ascot next time and Ryan Moore’s mount led her 24 rivals passing the half-furlong marker, only to be gunned down late on by one-length winner Libertango.

Undeterred, punters backed the Ballydoyle juvenile into 2-7 for the Group 2 Airlie Stud Stakes back at the Curragh just eight days on and they duly got their return, a three-quarter-length margin from Green Empress being scant reflection of the favourite’s superiority.

‌



That success made an ascent to the highest level the next logical move and Sun Goddess returned to the ‘Home of the Irish Classics’ for the Phoenix Stakes last Sunday week, beating Folsom Blues by a length and a quarter.

There’s a 7lb penalty to carry here but Sun Goddess sets the standard the others have to aim for and is expected to go in again. Tokaido is putting together a tidy CV in France and is feared, in company with Satellite Of Love and Vollering.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 SUN GODDESS, 2 TOKAIDO, 3 VOLLERING

View 7 Images Hamad Al Jehani: trains Newsboy's pick (Image: PA)

‌



3.00 Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 in 7 Grand Finale Handicap - BLUE BROTHER didn’t come up to expectations at Glorious Goodwood but is worth another chance.

Only 3-1 favourite Indalo preceded the Hamad Al Jehani-saddled five-year-old in the betting for the 18-runner Golden Mile on the South Downs - Blue Brother went off the 5-1 second choice.

Leading early on under James Doyle, the gelded son of Intello raced in second before fading through the final furlong to pass the post in eighth place behind his winning stablemate Archivist.

A reproduction of that form will send his backers home with empty pockets, but Blue Brother is better judged on his stable debut, and first outing for exactly a year, at Royal Ascot the previous month.

‌



Backed into 9-2 joint-favouritism for the seven-furlong Buckingham Palace Handicap, Blue Brother raced with enthusiasm and finished with gusto to take fourth, beaten two necks and three-quarters of a length, behind Mezcala.

Rain wouldn’t be an issue for a horse who has scored on heavy ground and, with the decision to stay at a mile almost certainly the correct one, Blue Brother is well capable of showing to the fore.

In an open heat, defending champion Bullet Point was back to form at the Shergar Cup and has podium claims, along with The Lost King and Arctic Dawn.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 BLUE BROTHER, 2 THE LOST KING, 3 ARCTIC DAWN

‌



View 7 Images Johanna Walsh: Newsboy's tip in the Yorkshire Oaks (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

3.35 Legend Global Yorkshire Oaks - JOHANNA WALSH is the value alternative to hot favourite Kalpana.

Joseph O’Brien hasn’t taken long to establish himself as a major player at the highest level, and the same can be said of Johanna Walsh.

Third in fillies’ maidens at Thurles and Gowran Park either side of the seasonal break, Sea The Stars’ daughter made it third time lucky with a three-and-a-quarter-length supremacy in a similar event at Leopardstown before her sights were raised to Group level.

‌



First up was the Group 2 Ribblesdale Stakes at Royal Ascot, for which my selection went off at 9-1 in a field of 12.

Never far from the action under Dylan Browne McMonagle, Johanna Walsh straightened for home in front but was unable to resist the late thrust of Earth Shot, who took the spoils by a head.

The pair reopposed in the Irish Oaks at the Curragh a month later but this time it was Johanna Walsh who came out on top, moving smoothly into the lead two furlongs out before shooting four lengths clear of Inis Mor, with Sparan Nua third and Earth Shot only sixth.

That emphatic triumph is unlikely to be Johanna Walsh last in the top tier, especially with more to come on the sixth start of her life.

‌



Kalpana comes here on the back of a thrilling King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes success and is greatly respected, with defending champion Minnie Hauk and Legacy Link also in the mix.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 JOHANNA WALSH, 2 KALPANA, 3 INIS MOR

View 7 Images John Gosden: co-trainer of Morrophore (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

4.10 British EBF & Sir Henry Cecil Galtres Stakes - MORROPHORE, taking on Listed opposition on her first start for seven months, is interesting.

‌



Nobody would describe the Kingman mare, trained in tandem by John and Thady Gosden, as equine poetry in motion - Morrophore flashes her tail and can look unwilling under pressure.

But only a hard audience would deny the five-year-old is a progressive performer - she has won four of her eight races, with the promise of better to come.

Unraced at two, Morrophore landed a novice stakes for fillies at Wolverhampton as a three-year-old in October 2024, doubling up in the handicap sphere at Ascot the following May.

Ryan Moore’s mount put a third win on her CV with a half-length call in the Winter Oaks Trial Fillies’ Handicap over 10 furlongs at Lingfield Park last December. And she returned to Surrey to capture the real thing in January, arriving just in the nick of time to shade Sky Safari by a head.

‌



Although she takes a rise in class, Morrophore is the best horse in this race according to the British Horseracing Authority figures and the fact she is a half-sister to three winners over a mile and a half augurs well for this step up in distance.

A La Prochaine, a 10-length fourth to Thundering On in the Oaks on her latest outing, is taken to fight it out with Vauntingly and Sunshine Star for the minor medals.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 MORROPHORE, 2 A LA PROCHAINE, 3 VAUNTINGLY

View 7 Images George Boughey: trainer of Mirzimaan (Image: PA)

‌



4.45 Mews Hotel Ossett EBF Stallions Nursery Handicap - MIRZIMAAN receives the vote to prove well treated as he makes his debut in the handicap milieu.

There is plenty to like about my selection’s pedigree - sire Mohaather was a Group 1-winning miler while dam Altaayshah didn’t make it to the track but is a sister to star sprinter Battaash. His blue-blooded ancestry counted for nothing when Mirzimaan trailed home last of 13 when a 16-1 chance for a six-furlong novice stakes at Newmarket in May.

But my selection clearly learned plenty from that experience - 55 days later, Mirzimaan took on 17 opponents for a similar event at Newbury and beat them all, containing Minster Boy by a length and a quarter.

And he was unlucky not to follow up under a penalty at Newcastle on his most recent outing, finding plenty of trouble in running before he steamed home for a short-head second to Asander.

‌



The step up from six furlongs to seven is a plus, and an opening British Horseracing Authority mark of 82 there for the taking. Dangers lurk at every turn in this full-field nursery, with Perfect Nation, Revels, Bymiddaytomorrow and Telegraphic just four juveniles whose best days lie ahead of them.

View 7 Images Oisin Orr (centre); rides Newsboy's selection (Image: Bahrain Turf Club/Racingfotos.com)

5.20 British EBF Fillies' Handicap - OOLONG POOBONG looks up to rewarding each-way support - at the very least.

A fine fourth in the Sandringham Fillies’ Handicap at Royal Ascot in June 2025 proved to be the Ed Bethell-trained daughter of Make Believe’s final start of last season. Oolong Poobong has met with defeat in both outings during the current campaign, but that doesn’t tell the whole story.

‌



She was entitled to come on for her reappearance, a perfectly respectable fifth at Thirsk in mid-May, after an absence of 330 days.

And a stall-three draw for the Kensington Palace Handicap for fillies and mares at Royal Ascot effectively snuffed out her chance - Jamie Spencer steered a path over to the stands’ side but Oolong Poobong couldn’t get involved, coming home in 20th.

Oisin Orr’s mount is better than she has been able to show so far this year and the step back from a mile won’t be a hindrance for a filly whose two career successes have been at six and seven furlongs. Oolong Poobong’s stablemate Caim, Secret History and and the returning Lam Yai all have something to recommend them.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 OOLONG POOBONG, 2 SECRET HISTORY, 3 CAIM

Sports.title: Man Utd haven't answered Harry Maguire's transfer plea as he makes Marcus Rashford demand
Sports.content:
Man Utd haven't answered Harry Maguire's transfer plea as he makes Marcus Rashford demand

Harry Maguire has made two requests to Manchester United this summer

View 2 Images Harry Maguire believes Manchester United must keep Marcus Rashford (Image: Marcel ter Bals/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Harry Maguire's transfer plea to Manchester United this summer has so far fallen on deaf ears. The Premier League side are now less than three days out from their season-opener away to Hull City in Saturday's early kick-off.

‌



It's been an unusually quiet window for United, who've signed just three first-team players. Michael Carrick has strengthened his side's midfield with the signings of Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £50million and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa for £35m.

‌



They also brought in goalkeeper Karl Darlow from Leeds United last month, with United yet to welcome any new arrivals since. At the time of the triple signing, which was confirmed in the space of two days, Maguire had called for even more signings to be made.

‌



The former United captain said to Sky Sports: "I played with Tielemans for a few months and he’s going to be an incredible signing, I have no doubt about that. He’s Belgium's captain and played most games for Aston Villa last season. He was a big player there.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Andrey Santos played yesterday [in the pre-season friendly against Wrexham]. He really impressed us in the first week and I think we’ve signed two great players there." The England defender added: "Hopefully more are coming through the door," before continuing: "As a player I want a big competitive squad. One that we can go and challenge for the big trophies so the more the merrier."

‌



Maguire has since doubled down on his stance, admitting he wants as many top players to join the club, despite the risk it'd have on his starting spot in Carrick's backline. He told Sky Sports: "When you play for this club, you want competition for places and it’s so important that we have a huge squad.

"I’m at an age now where they can bring in as many as they want, bring in all the best players. I want to win all the trophies and be greedy about it, but it’s up to the club."

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has yet to confirm whether Marcus Rashford will remain at Old Trafford (Image: Getty Images)

Sports.title: Arsenal would 'obviously consider' Ethan Nwaneri transfer as club chief spells out plan
Sports.content:
Arsenal would 'obviously consider' Ethan Nwaneri transfer as club chief spells out plan

Arsenal would be prepared to sell Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly with the two academy graduates facing uncertain futures at the Emirates

View 2 Images Arsenal have not ruled out the sale of Ethan Nwaneri (Image: Getty )

Arsenal's chief executive Richard Garlick has confessed that the club would consider offloading both Ethan Nwaneri and Myles Lewis-Skelly if "the right opportunity came up" - but they are "not actively looking to sell them".

‌



The Gunners boast one of Europe's best squads, which has had the likes of Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis added to it this summer, and that has seen certain players slip down the pecking order.

‌



Nwaneri was first given an opportunity by Mikel Arteta in 2022 and has had to be patient for his opportunities. He's shown his quality when given minutes and signed a long-term deal, but had to head out on loan to Marseille last season.

‌



Lewis-Skelly, meanwhile, has been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United, but did start for Arsenal in Sunday's Community Shield win. However, him and Nwaneri could both be moved on if the right offer comes in.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Garlick told BBC Sport: "There's been a lot of speculation around players. I can't stop other clubs being interested. I think Myles has had a fantastic end to last season and has started this one really well - we're very, very happy with him.

‌



"Ethan has had a great pre-season as well and I think it's just a case of looking at what opportunities there are that will help both of those in terms of their career moving forward. We are not actively looking at selling those homegrown players but if the right opportunity came up - right for them and the club - we'd obviously consider that."

Arsenal have signed Mikel Merino, Martin Zubimendi and Guimaraes in successive summers, which has ultimately impacted on Lewis-Skelly's hopes of forcing his way into a midfield role.

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly has been tipped to leave the Gunners (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Similarly, since Nwaneri made his Arsenal debut he's seen the likes of Noni Madueke, Eberechi Eze and Tzolis be signed by Arteta. Max Dowman has also emerged from the youth system.

The Arsenal boss has ultimately hinted at a departure for Nwaneri this summer as he claimed: "I want him to be at the club but something is in the medium-long term what is best for the player as well. Ethan needs to play football and if he stays here it's because we can guarantee that he can have those minutes."

Last term Nwaneri, who was only at the Emirates for half a season, failed to start a single Premier League game with just six substitute cameos. Lewis-Skelly meanwhile made 20 appearances, but only five of those were as a starter.

Sports.title: Premier League 3pm TV blackout could get SCRAPPED with talks to be held over streaming
Sports.content:
Premier League 3pm TV blackout could get SCRAPPED with talks to be held over streaming

The Premier League and EFL 3pm blackout could be in the process of getting scrapped with talks to be held ahead of a final decision

View 2 Images The Premier League 3pm blackout could be scrapped (Image: Getty Images)

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has revealed a decision on ending the 3pm blackout could be made before the end of the 2027/28 season.

‌



Currently, top-flight matches in England cannot be broadcast live on live domestic television between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on a Saturday afternoon. The tradition, which was enforced by the FA at the request of the EFL in the 1960s, is known as the '3pm blackout'.

‌



But there is talk that it could be removed when the next TV rights deal is finalised in 2028. The current cycle is due to expire at the end of the 2028/29 season. With that, a potential removal of the blackout would not be able to be introduced until the start of the 2029/30 campaign.

‌



Despite that wait, Masters has suggested progress is being made on ending the 3pm blackout and allowing all Premier League and EFL matches to be made available to broadcast.

Asked if English football is leaning towards the end of the blackout, Masters told talkSPORT: "Yes, but it's not just us involved in the decision about Article 48. It's us, the EFL and the FA.

"We've got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change. It's not a decision for now. It's a decision we've got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.

‌



View 2 Images Richard Masters (Image: Getty Images)

"I'd say in about 18 months' time we'll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not."

Masters' comments come after the Premier League launched a new streaming service in Singapore.

‌



'Premier League +' is poised to broadcast all 380 matches live and provide 24/7 coverage, in what is believed to be a testing ground for potential future streaming in the United Kingdom.

Simon Jordan, the talkSPORT presenter, has long called for the Premier League to have its own 'Netflix of Football' subscription service.

Sports.title: Barcelona ready to pounce as Harry Kane makes contract stance clear to Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Barcelona ready to pounce as Harry Kane makes contract stance clear to Bayern Munich

Harry Kane has entered the final year of his contract with Bayern Munich and the England captain is attracting interest from Barcelona in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Harry Kane has entered the final year of his Bayern Munich contract (Image: Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images)

Barcelona are reportedly ready to move for Harry Kane if his contract talks with Bayern Munich don't go to plan. Kane has entered the final year of his deal with Bayern, who are aware of interest from elsewhere in the England captain.

‌



Kane has scored a ludicrous 146 goals in 147 appearances since joining Bayern from Tottenham in a £86.4million deal in the summer of 2023. He is now 33 years old, but is showing no signs of slowing down as the most prolific goalscorer in Europe.

‌



Bayern are ready to offer Kane fresh terms to keep him in Bavaria and the need for action is clear. The Daily Mail reports that Barca are monitoring the situation and have made their interest known.

‌



Kane is seeking a three-year deal to extend his stay in Germany and could use Barcelona's interest, and that of Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal, as a bargaining chip.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Barcelona have signed Anthony Gordon, Rodri and Karim Adeyemi so far this summer, but could do with another forward after selling Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain and allowing Robert Lewandowski to leave upon the expiry of his contract. At this stage it seems unlikely that Barca could muscle in on Kane's talks with Bayern.

‌



"We obviously said we wanted to talk after the World Cup and after my holiday," Kane said this week. "So I'm not sure exactly when, but they'll start this week, next week... we'll start those talks. Like I've said before, we're calm, I think they're calm with the situation.

"Obviously now is the time to start talking, because there's only a year left. That's important. But both sides are relaxed, and I'm pretty sure there'll be some talks this week or next week."

View 2 Images Harry Kane is happy at Bayern Munich and is about to enter contract talks (Image: Leonhard Simon/Getty Images)

‌



He scored 61 goals in 51 appearances in all competitions last season as Vincent Kompany's side completed a league and cup double. And his form is such that Kane is a contender for the Ballon d'Or.

"The Ballon d'Or is as big as it gets, from an individual point of view," he said. "I know I had a great season last season, but the focus is on this new season.

"The Ballon d'Or's not in my hands. I've done what I can do in terms of putting in the performances. It's now down to votes and other people and the media - stuff I can't control - so we'll see what happens.

Article continues below

"Obviously, it would be amazing if it was to happen. But ultimately, it's still two or three months away before that's decided so it's not something that's at the front of my mind right now."

Sports.title: Ezri Konsa could make Arsenal debut at Aston Villa after £51m transfer agreement struck
Sports.content:
Ezri Konsa could make Arsenal debut at Aston Villa after £51m transfer agreement struck

Ezri Konsa is closing in on a move to Arsenal after Aston Villa look hands on a deal with their Premier League counterparts for the England defender

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is poised for a move to Arsenal (Image: Getty)

Ezri Konsa is expected to undergo a medical at Arsenal tomorrow after the Gunners struck a deal worth in the region of £50million plus add-ons for the England international.

‌



Konsa, who grew up supporting Tottenham, pushed for the move following an extended break after the World Cup.

‌



Premier League champions Arsenal are not expected to beat Thursday's 12pm registration deadline in time for Konsa to feature in their opener against Coventry City on Friday, though his fitness still requires work anyway after Unai Emery handed him four full weeks of rest alongside Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez.

‌



It means there is a firm chance that Konsa, providing all formalities go to plan, could well make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park - the ground he has called home for the past seven seasons - on August 31.

Mikel Arteta has been absolutely set on signing the 28-year-old, who was his top defensive target and had a new lucrative contract on the table in the Midlands, despite interest in various other centre-backs including Jarell Quansah, Cristian Romero and free agent John Stones.

Jose Mourinho rubbishes Rodri claim after Real Madrid lose transfer battle to Barcelona READ MORE :

Arsenal dynasty predicted as one promoted team backed to survive Premier League READ MORE :

Konsa can also operate as a a right-back and is viewed as a plug-and-play signing, much like £75m arrival Bruno Guimaraes, that bolsters Arsenal's depth in the absence of William Saliba - absent with a long-term back problem.

‌



The Gunners initially made a £30m approach for Konsa earlier this summer which was immediately dismissed before returning to the table last week and communicating their desire to reach £40m for the player.

However, Villa continued to hold firm on their £60m asking price until Konsa, who had two years left on his existing deal, made it clear he was determined to pursue the opportunity and return to London, where he previously played for Brentford and Charlton Athletic.

He is on course to become Arsenal's fifth summer acquisition after Piero Hincapie (his loan from Bayer Leverkusen became permanent), Illan Meslier, Christos Tzolis and Guimaraes, which would take their spending to around £194.5m.

‌



View 2 Images Ezri Konsa was a mainstay for England at the World Cup (Image: Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Konsa - set for a substantial pay-rise - will also become the latest high-profile Villa sale after Youri Tielemans ( Manchester United ), Morgan Rogers ( Chelsea ) and Lucas Digne ( PSG ) while Watkins and Martinez are also facing uncertain futures at the club.

Watkins is wanted by Al-Hilal, who have had three approaches rebuffed to date.

Article continues below

Another factor in Arsenal's decision to sign Konsa is that he's a homegrown player. Having eight homegrown players registered will enable them to officially name a 25-man Premier League squad. Winger Gabriel Martinelli currently classifies as homegrown but he could yet depart before the deadline.

If the Gunners were only able to list seven senior homegrown players, they would only be able to register a 24-man squad.
