World.title: Clément, el hijo no reconocido de Lorenzo de Bélgica durante años, ya es príncipe
World.content:
El sobrino del rey Felipe fue reconocido oficialmente por su padre en septiembre de 2025, poco antes de contar su historia en un documental. Ahora ya tiene el título, pero este no le reportará dotación económica ni un lugar en la línea de sucesión

Clément Vandenkerckhove, el hijo no reconocido durante 25 años del siempre polémico príncipe Lorenzo de Bélgica —hermano menor del rey Felipe—, se ha convertido oficialmente en príncipe de Bélgica, según ha informado este miércoles la prensa belga. Este título llega tras décadas de rumores, pero tan solo un año después desde el reconocimiento del joven por parte de su padre, el 9 de septiembre de 2025, y a los pocos meses desde que en febrero de este año Lorenzo de Bélgica formalizara el reconocimiento legal de paternidad.

“En los últimos años, hemos discutido abierta y honestamente esta cuestión. El anuncio se realiza con la comprensión y respeto hacia las partes implicadas y es el resultado de un acuerdo”, confesó el príncipe Lorenzo en el comunicado en el que reconoció su paternidad. Pocos días después de ese anuncio, el diario local Het Laatste Nieuws publicó que el rey Felipe de Bélgica le concedería el título de príncipe al hijo, hasta entonces secreto, de su hermano, lo que desde este 19 de agosto es una realidad.

La existencia de Clément salió a la luz en septiembre de 2025, cuando el propio príncipe Lorenzo —hijo del antiguo rey Alberto II— confirmó que había tenido un hijo antes de casarse con la princesa Clara. La revelación llegó tan solo un día antes de que el propio Clément hablara públicamente por primera vez sobre la identidad de su padre, poniendo fin a años de secreto, en un documental en el canal de televisión VTM.

Clément Vandenkerckhove y su madre, Wendy Van Wanten, en una imagen del documental 'Clément, zoon van'. Premiere Pro (VTM)

El joven, de 26 años, es fruto de un noviazgo entre Lorenzo de Bélgica y la modelo y cantante Wendy Van Wanten —cuyo verdadero nombre es Iris Vandenkerckhove—, y su nacimiento tuvo lugar en el año 2000, antes de que Lorenzo de Bélgica se comprometiera, en 2003, con su esposa Claire Coombs (la princesa Clara), madre de sus tres hijos, Louise, Nicolás y Aymeric, con quienes ahora pasa a ser heredero de Lorenzo en igualdad de condiciones.

No es el primer caso parecido en la familia real belga. Este recuerda al de Delphine Boël —ahora Delfina de Sajonia-Coburgo—, que tras años de batalla judicial logró en 2020 ser reconocida como hija de Alberto II y obtuvo el título de princesa. A pesar de ser miembro con pleno derecho de la casa real belga, en 2023, tras ser excluida de los eventos de la familia real, reclamó al primer ministro del país por no recibir el mismo trato que sus hermanos, hijos del rey Alberto II y la reina Paola.

En ambos casos, el título no conlleva función oficial ni rango protocolario ni da derecho a dotación económica. Su acceso al trono queda además descartado, ya que no forman parte de la línea sucesoria de la dinastía. El reconocimiento también les da derecho a usar el apellido dinástico de Sajonia-Coburgo, aunque el propio Clément ha dicho en el pasado que prefiere mantener el apellido de su madre, Vandenkerckhove, y que, si acepta algo de la familia real, lo haría como nombre compuesto con “de Bélgica”.

Vandenkerckhove, que sí podrá reclamar el tratamiento de alteza, trabaja actualmente en la cocina de un restaurante y vive en Aalter, entre Gante y Brujas, según una entrevista reciente con el diario Het Nieuwsblad. En el documental en el que él mismo reveló su identidad como hijo de Lorenzo de Bélgica, admitió que su único deseo era “tomarse una cerveza con su padre y poder vivir una vida normal”. “Mi padre no hizo nada malo, mi madre no hizo nada malo. No quiero oír constantemente: ¿Sabes siquiera quién es tu padre?’, ‘¿Ya murió?’. Quiero acabar con eso”, revelaba entonces. El pasado 14 de junio, Día del Padre en Bélgica, él mismo publicó en su perfil de Instagram, con cerca de 5.500 seguidores, una foto actual con su padre biológico y otra, de niño, con Frans Vancoppenolle, marido de Van Wanten: “Hoy quiero rendir homenaje a dos padres que, cada uno a su manera, desempeñan un papel importante en mi vida. Gracias por todo. ¡Feliz Día del Padre!“, escribió junto a ellas.

World.title: La muerte del profesor de Cambridge Jason Arday resucita la guerra cultural en la universidad británica
World.content:
Jason Arday a su llegada al programa 'Domingo con Laura Kuenssberg' de la BBC, el 30 de marzo de 2025.

La triste historia de Jason Arday, el exprofesor de Sociología de la Educación de la Universidad de Cambridge hallado muerto el pasado viernes en su apartamento londinense de Battersea, es una fábula que destapa varias capas de conflicto moral, ético y político.

Es la prueba de la desesperación de las instituciones académicas británicas por incorporar a su profesorado celebridades que las hagan más atractivas, rebajando su nivel de exigencia. Es también una muestra del irracional afán de revancha de una derecha reaccionaria contra lo que considera años de injusto wokismo (la promoción de la igualdad y avance de las minorías en el ámbito laboral o académico). Es un despliegue de racismo mal disimulado por parte de esa derecha. Y es, sobre todo, la confirmación de que una determinada prensa del Reino Unido sigue viviendo de la carroña y es maestra en el cinismo.

Fue el legendario Kelvin MacKenzie, director del tabloide The Sun, quien se inventó la consigna Reverse Ferret (Marcha Atrás al Hurón), cuando era necesario dar un giro drástico a la línea editorial del periódico. Los mineros de Yorkshire competían entre ellos metiéndose en los pantalones un hurón, un mamífero pequeño, flexible y ágil como una descarga eléctrica cuando entra en agujeros o madrigueras, para comprobar quién resistía más sus sacudidas. MacKenzie aseguraba que la tarea de todo periodista es meter un hurón en la entrepierna de cada personaje público. Hasta que la presión social da un giro y se vuelve en contra del medio. Entonces toca sacar al bicho.

Este domingo, el tabloide Daily Mail destacaba los más de 150.000 euros recaudados ya por la familia del profesor para combatir el racismo, y la bandera a media asta que ondea en el Jesus College, donde Arday daba clases. El diario, que se mofó de él estos días con crueldad, presentaba ahora al profesor, con un tono condescendiente, como la víctima de un sistema que lo colocó en una posición por encima de sus capacidades, “hasta que el mundo se le vino encima”.

En las semanas previas, el Mail había ridiculizado hasta el absurdo los supuestos plagios académicos, y exageraciones o falsedades biográficas de Arday, en un tono que muchos críticos, como Simon Woolley, director del Homerton College de Cambridge, han denunciado como una “caza de brujas racista”.

Miles de manifestantes se han concentrado este lunes ante la National Gallery, en la céntrica plaza londinense de Trafalgar, convocados por la asociación Stand Up To Racism (Planta Cara al Racismo), para celebrar una vigilia en recuerdo del profesor, y para exigir una investigación pública sobre lo que consideran una campaña de racismo exacerbado que acabó con su vida.

Estudiantes y personal universitario rinden homenaje a Jason Arday frente la Casa del Senado, el domingo. Nordin Catic (Getty Images)

Una historia exagerada

Arday fue un niño diagnosticado con autismo que —según él mismo contó— no empezó a hablar hasta los once años, y aprendió a leer y escribir a los dieciocho. A los 37 años, fue nombrado el profesor titular de raza negra más joven en la historia de la Universidad de Cambridge. La revista estadounidense The Atlantic llegó a definirle como “el sociólogo más famoso del mundo”.

Su vida era un modelo de esfuerzo y superación, un póster de la escalera social del mérito. Nacido en 1985, en el barrio londinense de Clapham, Jason Atta Kwei Arday era hijo de un chef y una cuidadora de pacientes de salud mental procedentes de Ghana.

Aunque empezó sus estudios universitarios con ambiciones modestas, preparándose en Educación Física (el deporte se le dio bien desde pequeño) en la Universidad de St. Mary, en Twickenham, el mundo académico estimuló su curiosidad y sus habilidades de escritura. Un máster en Educación y Pedagogía le permitió ingresar en el claustro de la Universidad de John Moores, en Liverpool, donde logró finalmente su doctorado.

Su progreso académico ascendente era paralelo a su popularidad como deportista especializado en recaudar fondos benéficos, a base de maratones sobrehumanos y objetivos casi imposibles. El tenista Andy Murray llegó a declarar su admiración por Arday, que en 2012 fue uno de los portadores de la antorcha olímpica de los Juegos de Londres.

Con escritos centrados en la raza y la neurodiversidad racial en el mundo universitario, el joven profesor ascendía escalones en distintas instituciones (puestos en las universidades de Roehampton, Durham o Glasgow), y el pináculo de su carrera fue el salto a Cambridge, contratado por el Jesus College.

Estudiantes a las puertas del Jesus College de Cambridge,el 7 de agosto TOLGA AKMEN (EFE)

Llegó a recibir más de 200.000 correos de felicitación procedentes de todo el mundo, pero también miles de cartas cuajadas de odio que ponían en cuestión sus méritos y señalaban el color de su piel como la razón de tan vertiginoso ascenso.

Ya debía intuir la tormenta que le esperaba más adelante, cuando en abril de este año, durante una conferencia en la celebración del 75º aniversario de la Asociación de Sociólogos Británicos, Arday denunció las maniobras de una “derecha activista” que usaba espuriamente los mecanismos diseñados para proteger la integridad académica en una campaña contra los profesores de raza negra.

Plagios y falsedades

Las primeras acusaciones se centraron en su tesis doctoral. El diario conservador The Daily Telegraph señaló hasta cien pasajes del texto muy similares a la publicación que había realizado seis años antes Paula Zowzdiak-Myers, una estudiante de la Universidad de Brunel, en Londres. Aunque la John Moores de Liverpool, donde Arday obtuvo el doctorado, rechazó las acusaciones de plagio y atribuyó esos pasajes a “errores honestos y razonables”, la cacería contra el profesor comenzó a fraguarse en la derecha mediática y académica.

Tenían ganchos a los que aferrarse. Arday había presumido de puestos universitarios honorarios falsos o exagerados, que los medios británicos fueron incapaces de confirmar, o de libros que nunca fueron realmente publicados.

Su vida y su pasado fueron escrutados con microscopio. Las hazañas deportivas de las que presumía, como los 30 maratones en 30 días, o las 600 millas (965 kilómetros) en seis días, todo cuestionado por médicos y expertos en la materia. O sus historias de los abusos racistas sufridos en el ámbito académico (que realmente sufrió), exagerados con la denuncia de ataques con cuchillo y hasta el envío a su casa de una cabeza de cerdo que la policía nunca confirmó.

Todos aquellos que han hecho estos años bandera de la lucha contra el wokismo se frotaban las manos. El profesor estadounidense Nathan Cofnas, promotor de infames teorías de racismo científico que llegó a afirmar que la Universidad de Harvard no tendría ni un solo profesor negro si fuera solo por mérito académico, fue expulsado del Emmanuel College de Cambridge por sus desvaríos, y la semana pasada celebraba como una “venganza cristiana” la caída de Arday, y se proclamaba responsable de sacar a la luz las falsedades del profesor.

Según los datos publicados el año pasado por la Agencia de Estadísticas de Educación Superior, solo 75 de las 6.180 personas que componen el claustro de Cambridge se definen como de raza negra. Profesores titulares, como Arday, solo había cinco, incluido él mismo. La realidad niega los prejuicios.

La Universidad de Cambridge, señalada por esa derecha como uno de los ejemplos de instituciones liberales decadentes, víctimas de la diversidad e integración, comenzó defendiendo a Arday. Pronto, sin embargo, viró de rumbo y abrió una investigación.

El profesor dimitió el 5 de agosto. Diez días después, la policía halló su cadáver en su domicilio. Estaba casado y tenía dos hijos. Hasta el final de sus días rechazó las acusaciones de plagio. “Jason Arday fue la víctima de una perniciosa campaña de deshonra que otros en su posición no habrían sufrido. Su muerte es una tragedia, y debe ser una llamada de atención para todos”, ha dicho el alcalde laborista y musulmán de Londres, Sadiq Khan, uno de los muchos que ha denunciado el inmenso racismo, amparado por las exageraciones y medias verdades de Arday (como tantos otros), que ha revelado este caso.

El primer ministro de Reino Unido, Andy Burnham, lamentó el sábado la muerte de Arday, que todavía está siendo investigada como un posible suicidio, y realizó un llamamiento a la calma. “No es momento para juicios precipitados. Es un momento para la reflexión, diría yo, para reflexionar sobre cómo se llegó a esta situación”, dijo.

World.title: ‘Moria’: una serie ‘mostra’ para la ‘mostra’ mayor
World.content:
Artículos estrictamente de opinión que responden al estilo propio del autor. Estos textos de opinión han de basarse en datos verificados y ser respetuosos con las personas aunque se critiquen sus actos. Todas las columnas de opinión de personas ajenas a la Redacción de EL PAÍS llevarán, tras la última línea, un pie de autor —por conocido que éste sea— donde se indique el cargo, título, militancia política (en su caso) u ocupación principal, o la que esté o estuvo relacionada con el tema abordado

A pesar de sus recién cumplidos 80 años y sus más de 55 de exitosa carrera, la distancia ha hecho de la vedette, actriz, presentadora y celebridad todoterreno argentina Moria Casán alguien poco conocido en España. Sospecho que a muchos por aquí les generaría rechazo esa picardía tan suya –y tan nuestra– pasada por la túrmix del ecosistema televisivo argentino, que deja en pañales a los programas más macarras de nuestra historia televisiva. Para acercarla a nuestra latitud, se la podría definir como una mezcla entre Susana Estrada, Lola Flores y Belén Esteban: erotismo, carisma, ingenio, frontalidad y frases lapidarias. Pero me quedaría corta, porque Moria no se parece a nadie. Si en algo se ha empeñado a lo largo de su trayectoria es en cultivar una personalidad única y en –si me permiten el palabro– performarla y retorcerla hasta el paroxismo.

Netflix acaba de estrenar Moria, su serie biográfica. Un género que tiene más peligros que considerar a Marcos Llorente una autoridad dermatológica. Primero porque decantar una vida para armar un relato ya, de entrada, suele plantear contradicciones de base: hay vidas llenas de acontecimientos extraordinarios que no tienen el más mínimo interés dramático y personajes extraordinarios cuyas vidas carecen de recorrido narrativo. Segundo, porque si tras él está su protagonista, puede convertirse en una hagiografía impúdica. Y tercero, porque es fácil caer en el síndrome Wikipedia (querer contarlo todo y por el camino olvidarse de contar algo). Y cuarto, por la dificultad de hermanar al público, desde el fan hasta el ajeno al personaje.

Moria es una serie excesiva, delirante, frívola e histriónica. Esto es, como su propia protagonista, a quien le encanta definirse como mostra. Así pues, esta ristra de adjetivos, lejos de constituir un demérito, pueden considerarse, en mayor o menor medida, un halago, sobre todo si uno tiene interés por el personaje. ¿Café para muy cafeteros? Mate para muy materos. Brilla más cuanto más se aleja de los acontecimientos históricos (para pintar una dictadura de cartón piedra mejor ni pintarla) y de la santificación vía icono LGTBIQ+ y cuanto más se deja arrollar por sus elementos fantásticos y las contradicciones del personaje, interpretado en sus tres etapas por Sofía Gala Castiglione (que espero cuente con un buen terapeuta tras haber interpretado a su madre), Griselda Siciliani (mi favorita, protagonista de la época más suculenta) y Cecilia Roth. A las tres las sobrevuela la propia Moria, como una giganta que domina el decorado –“¡El decorado se calla!”, que diría ella misma–. Una serie mostra para la mostra mayor.

World.title: Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj
World.content:
Este enclave del Baix Empordà ha logrado conservar la magia de sus playas y calas, goza de algunas de las mejores propuestas culinarias del territorio y atrae por igual a locales y foráneos, permaneciendo en un ventajoso segundo plano a la hora de atraer al turismo masivo

Begur es una localidad catalana cuya fundación los historiadores acostumbran a situar en 1019, con la construcción del castillo de la localidad, aunque sus inicios datan de la época feudal. Ubicada a apenas 30 kilómetros de Girona, esta joya del Baix Empordà consigue permanecer alejada durante gran parte del año de las rutas turísticas masificadas que recorren parajes como Barcelona, la siempre bulliciosa Costa Brava o ciertas zonas del Empordà. Conserva además intacta su capacidad para sorprender al viajero y acumula un buen número de razones que obligan al habitual a seguir volviendo a su calma chicha. En verano la cosa cambia y la población, de apenas 4.000 habitantes, se multiplica por diez, pero, aun así, el pueblo se las ingenia para seguir siendo (relativamente) tranquilo.

Sa Punta, un establecimiento familiar totalmente remodelado de la mano de un grupo de empresarios encabezados por Daniela McLean —ideóloga del proyecto y con amplia experiencia en leyendas de la hostelería de lujo como el Palace Hôtel de Crillon, en París, o el grupo Peninsula Hotels—, se ha convertido en uno de los grandes imanes de esta localidad de cielos limpios y carácter familiar, con su apariencia de casa señorial en cuyo interior se esconde el espíritu de una beach house pensada para apagar el móvil, desenchufar el ordenador y vivir como si el mundo exterior hubiera decidido dejarnos en paz durante unos días.

Más información 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde

El jardín del hotel Sa Punta, en Begur.

Este hotel cuenta con 36 habitaciones, un spa, un restaurante con vocación transversal y sin delirios de grandeza (hay arroces, pero también hamburguesas), una piscina perfecta para los que desean ponerse en remojo en lugar de encaminarse hacia la playa y un entorno donde predomina el verde y una tranquilidad casi desconcertante, teniendo en cuenta los desquiciantes parámetros urbanitas. “Estamos en un lugar emblemático, rodeado de campos, de viñedos y de rutas ideales para darse una vuelta en bici o un buen paseo. Es un hotel muy tranquilo porque hacemos yoga y es solo para adultos. Siempre digo que es un hotel que transmite calma: pensado para desconectar totalmente del estrés. Por eso muchas veces insistimos en lo de la beach house para explicar por qué esto no es un hotel de lujo al uso ni un cuatro estrellas convencional”, explica Sandra Julià, la directora del establecimiento. “Tampoco estamos en primera línea de mar, aunque en cinco minutos puedas plantarte en la playa. Es una zona más elevada, así que tenemos unas vistas preciosas, pero con un ambiente mucho más íntimo”, añade sobre este establecimiento que abre de abril a octubre para adaptarse a las necesidades y deseos de su clientela.

La dificultad de acceder a Begur si uno no dispone de coche (el transporte público funciona en la temporada estival, pero sigue siendo complejo acceder al pueblo) se ha convertido, paradójicamente, en una de las ventajas de la localidad. “Totalmente. Lo cierto es que la gran mayoría de nuestros clientes necesitan coche para llegar hasta aquí y está claro que, si fuera accesible con el tren, el autobús y el transporte público, sería muy diferente. Y no solo para el hotel, para toda la zona. La movilidad aquí ya es complicada. Es cierto que a Begur y a Pals puedes llegar en autobús, pero no llega el tren. Eso hace que sea un destino un poco más exclusivo”, confirma Julià.

Vista del castillo de Begur. BORIS STROUJKO (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Más allá de las virtudes de un alojamiento pensado para el reposo y la desconexión, si uno decide salir de Sa Punta, Begur ofrece una triada insuperable: gastronomía, paseos y un sinfín de destellos del pasado. “Creo que eso es precisamente lo que la gente viene buscando. Pueblos medievales como Pals o Peratallada, lugares históricos, una gastronomía increíble, el arroz de Pals y unas playas preciosas. Todas esas pequeñas calas llenas de encanto”, aporta Julià. Pero a pesar del innegable atractivo de la geografía y la idiosincrasia que recorre cada rincón del Baix Empordà, Julià reconoce que algunos de sus clientes vienen buscando cosas distintas: “Por supuesto, hay de todo y también nos gusta que sea así, tener muchos perfiles distintos y ser capaces de atenderles con la misma solvencia. Hay clientes que vienen únicamente a jugar al golf. Comen aquí todos los días y no quieren hacer nada más. O los ciclistas, que pasan el día entero sobre la bicicleta. ¡Hay de todo!”, sonríe.

Para que no queden dudas, la directora de Sa Punta deja claro que en el hotel se prioriza un enfoque centrado en el adulto. El establecimiento es un gran reclamo para el turista familiar, pero solo con adolescentes, ya que la edad mínima son 12 años. “Por eso tenemos muchas parejas o grupos de amigos que vienen a darse un homenaje culinario, y no hay niños, pero pueden traerse a sus perros… siempre que no pesen más de nueve kilos”, aclara.

El bar exterior del hotel Sa Punta.

Para ponerse las botas

Lo del buen comer es casi una obligación para cualquiera que visite este enclave gerundense. La oferta es amplia, el producto impecable y hay un buen número de lugares que parecen sacados de una de esas películas románticas en las que los protagonistas se ponen las botas con el mar de fondo. AlKostat del Mar (en el hotel Finca Victoria) es uno de esos paraísos: con un coloso como el chef Jordi Vilà, responsable de los fogones de dos templos barceloneses como el Alkimia y Alkostat al mando del establecimiento, esta se ha convertido en una de las citas imprescindibles para los amantes de la buena mesa.

El chef Jordi Vilà está al frente de AlKostat del Mar, en el hotel Finca Victoria.

“AlKostat del Mar es un proyecto que puede adaptarse al territorio y es totalmente permeable a la cocina local. Casi podríamos decir que por sedimentación se acomoda allí donde llega. Creo que hacemos una cocina muy fresca, muy de olores, muy de sabores, sencilla: catalana y tradicional, pero siempre con nuestro toque. Como trabajamos mucho con el producto de temporada, pues hay mucho tomate y mucho pescado a la brasa”, explica Vilà. ¿Un plato imprescindible? “La ensaladilla rusa a la brasa, en la que cada ingrediente pasa por las brasas antes de volver al plato. Creo que explica muy bien lo que hacemos”.

Por supuesto, la competencia es feroz y en la lista de los favoritos de la localidad también sacan la cabeza tótems como Cap Sa Sal y la sidrería Mooma. Si hay ganas de aventura, Far Nomo, en Llafranc, es otra recomendación de primera clase y localidades como Peratallada, Pals y Calella de Palafrugell también ofrecen una gran variedad de mesas en las que ponerse las botas.

Para los amantes de los paseos o las calas, Begur es un seguro de vida: en el camino que lleva de Aiguablava a Platja Fonda puede recorrerse uno de los tramos más bellos del Camí de Ronda de la Costa Brava. El sendero transcurre entre pinos y acantilados, enlazando pequeñas calas y miradores naturales con vistas al Mediterráneo. El recorrido culmina en la mencionada Platja Fonda, una playa de arena oscura encajada entre altas paredes rocosas que sigue conservando una atmósfera casi mágica.

Si uno se queda con ganas de más, nada mejor que apostar por la ruta que lleva desde Cap de Begur a El Semàfor, un recorrido menos conocido que permite adentrarse en una de las zonas más agrestes del litoral de Begur. Un sendero que llega a una antigua estación electro-semafórica (la mencionada, El Semàfor), inaugurada en 1891 para orientar a los barcos de la Costa Brava. En el extremo del Cap de Begur, el edificio se abre hoy como mirador privilegiado sobre el mar.

Con tanto paseo, piscina, bici, golf y banquete, puede que en algún momento apetezca la irremediable tentación del dulce: para eso existe la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, uno de esos sitios a los que hay que ir dispuesto a dejarse aconsejar. “Abrí hace unos seis años y aposté desde el principio por la pastelería tradicional, pero reduciendo un 20% el azúcar. Abro todo el año y, aparte de brazos de gitano, coronas y pasteles como el de requesón (con queso local) o tiramisú con ratafía, mi producto estrella es el buñuelo del Empordà”, cuenta Anna Ferret, que regenta este palacete del dulce en la localidad gerundense.

Uno de los rulos de nata de la la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, en Begur.

La directora de Sa Punta quiere ofrecer a los interesados un último aliciente: “Tenemos un plus, que es algo que a mí me gusta mucho, y es que existe un gran sentimiento de comunidad que a su vez se traduce en una gran dosis de solidaridad: Sa punta forma parte de Costa Brava Centre y yo conozco a la mayoría de los directores de hoteles cercanos. Si tengo un banquete y me faltan sesenta platos, se los pido al hotel de al lado. Siempre nos ayudamos y eso me parece extraordinario en los tiempos que corren”. “Supongo que también es un buen modo de resumir lo que es Begur: un lugar en el que nunca te faltará de nada”, remata Julià.

World.title: Online sleuth links Amsterdam’s “Lucky” to Canadian cold case
World.content:
An online researcher may have made a breakthrough in the hunt for the identity of “Lucky”, a man who collapsed in Amsterdam three years ago and is unable to communicate. A recent public appeal for information by the police has surfaced a potential match with a missing person in Canada.

An image of “Lucky”, who was also known by the name “Chris the Canadian” to Amsterdam locals, was likened to a file of pictures on the Vancouver Police Department’s cold case unit by someone on Facebook.

John Russell Kennedy, whose missing person’s file photos appear very similar to the one the Dutch police put out, was registered as missing since 1993.

Dutch police said they are considering the tip, according to paper AD, though they also noted that such similarities have been common in prior cases and turned out not to be real matches. “We don’t want to jump to any conclusions at this point, or to give false hope,” a spokesperson said.

Much of what is listed on the Canadian missing person’s case matches descriptions put out by locals who knew the man before his collapse in 2023. He was said to have a North American accent and appeared to have mental health problems.

Vancouver police confirmed they are taking the tip very seriously and said they had made contact with Amsterdam police, according to Anton van Straten, the person who made the connection online and shared it via Facebook.

“Only an official investigation, for example using DNA, can provide certainty about this,” Van Straten wrote in his post. “Now it is up to the professionals to investigate this further. In any case, it didn’t take me three years to find this potential match.”

If “Lucky” is indeed John Russell Kennedy, he would be 67 years old now and missing from his family for almost half his life.

World.title: Number of non-EU dentists in NL doubles in five years
World.content:
The number of dentists trained outside the EU who are moving to the Netherlands to help fill a chronic national shortage has more than doubled in five years, with recent arrivals coming from countries including Syria, South Africa, Turkey, Brazil and Iraq.

One in four dentists now working in the country qualified abroad, according to the dentists’ association KNMT, and in Zeeland more than half were trained overseas.

Figures from the Amsterdam dental school ACTA, which runs the admissions process for applicants from outside the EU, show 120 people are sitting its professional competence test this year, compared with 53 in 2021, the current affairs programme Nieuwsuur reported.

In total, 2,287 dentists with a foreign diploma are working in the Netherlands, a number rising by 150 to 200 a year.

Lack of national funding

The reliance on overseas recruits is partly due to a lack of education funding for Dutch students. Thousands apply but places are very limited. Etienne Verheijck, education director for the ACTA, called that “a policy choice by the education ministry.”

KNMT chair Hans de Vries called it “painful” that motivated young people are rejected by a lottery system, sometimes three times in a row, while the gap is filled from abroad.

The shortage is expected to grow, and the government’s own capacity advisory body has for years urged ministers to open more training places.

Checking your dentist is registered

To work in the Netherlands, dentists with a non-EU diploma must pass a competence test and learn Dutch before they can join the official BIG register of healthcare professionals. Those with an EU diploma need only meet the language requirement.

The healthcare inspectorate IGJ said it regularly receives reports of people performing treatments such as root canals without being registered. De Vries said dentists may work under a registered colleague’s supervision while they qualify, but treating patients unsupervised is improper and potentially unlawful.

Patients can check whether their own dentist appears on the BIG register, which is public and free to search. Dental care in the Netherlands works differently from many other countries, and full practices unable to take on new patients are already a common complaint.

A 12-year-old Dutch boy is being treated in intensive care after falling 30 metres (100ft) while walking in the Austrian alps.

Local media reported that the boy was walking with his father when he slipped and fell while crossing rocky terrain in the Tirol mountain range at 11am on Tuesday.

The pair were descending the Gänsekragen mountain after reaching the 2,914m (9,560ft) summit at 9.30am.

They were walking along a waymarked path towards a mountain hut in Winnebachsee when the accident happened about 500m below the summit as the boy rounded a corner.

The 46-year-old man managed to climb down the hillside to his son, who was lying unconscious, and raise the alarm. An air ambulance transported him to a clinic in Innsbruck, where he is being treated for serious injuries.

Police are investigating how the boy fell.

World.title: Schiphol security staff begin strike action over workload
World.content:
Security staff at Schiphol will begin short work stoppages and deliberately slow-downs in the coming days, after the airport and its three security firms missed a union deadline to ease a workload the unions say has become unmanageable. Travellers could face longer queues as a result.

Unions FNV and CNV announced the action on Wednesday, after an ultimatum to Schiphol and the firms Securitas, I-SEC and Trigion expired at midday. The stoppages will be flagged only a few hours in advance, and the unions have not ruled out longer strikes if nothing changes.

“Nobody wants industrial action at Schiphol,” said CNV negotiator André Quist. “But if employers take no concrete step against the enormous workload even after a crystal-clear ultimatum, they leave our members no choice.”

The dispute dates back to a shake-up in the spring, when Schiphol cut the number of firms running hand-baggage checks from five to three. The switch to new employers affected most of the airport’s roughly 5,000 security guards, whose pay was preserved but whose rosters, shift times, breaks and leave all changed.

Since then, the unions say, workloads have risen and sickness absence has climbed, leaving fewer guards to carry the same load – a downward spiral they warn is getting worse.

In July the unions made eight demands, including longer breaks, two consecutive days off after five worked, a heat protocol for the terminals, and at least two women on every security lane so female passengers can be searched. A lane should close, they say, if only one woman is available.

Schiphol said it regretted the action and took the guards’ concerns seriously, adding that it and the three firms were already working on improvements to five of the eight demands. It said it would do all it could to limit the impact on travellers.

A separate walkout by around 350 cleaners at the airport also happened on Wednesday for two hours around midday in a dispute over reduced sick pay in the national cleaning agreement, which FNV wants Schiphol, as a major client, to help resist.

World.content:

Ajax fans who want to watch the club’s crucial Conference League play-off match against Swiss club Sion will have to pay €4.99 after the broadcasting rights were acquired by Talpa.

The match, which kicks off at 8.15pm on Thursday, is being shown on Talpa’s pay-per-view channel KIJK, angering many Dutch fans.

The decision also went down badly with Ziggo, Ajax’s main sponsor and one of the Netherlands’ biggest commercial sports broadcasters.

Ziggo has the exclusive rights to show matches in UEFA’s main competitions, but qualifying rounds are not covered by that deal.

The company posted a message on social media site X, formerly Twitter, explaining that Sion as the home club was entitled to sell the broadcasting rights to the highest bidder.

The return leg in Amsterdam next Thursday, August 27, will be screen on Ziggo’s free subscription channel.

World.title: Criminals cashing in on black market for non-deposit cans
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Criminal gangs are earning millions by importing canned drinks to bypass the Dutch deposit return system.

The black market has sprung up since a compulsory 15 cent deposit was imposed on all drinks cans in 2023, as part of the Dutch government’s plans to cut waste.

The environmental standards inspectorate ILT estimates that up to 50 million illegally imported bottles are sold every year, often in restaurants and cafés that buy them from illegal traders.

In an echo of the Netherlands’ cannabis policy, importing canned drinks is outlawed, but buying and selling them after they cross the border is not, making the drinks attractive to outlets that want to avoid the cost and logistical burden of recycling thousands of cans.

Soft drinks are bought from Germany and Denmark, while beer is more commonly imported from Poland, all countries in the border-free Schengen zone.

The result is that the cans end up in landfill or as litter, hampering the government’s efforts to meet its recycling targets.

“It’s an illegal trade,” ILT acting inspector-general Edwin van Houten told EenVandaag. “They come into contact with organised crime because there is a huge amount of money to be earned from avoiding the rules. It runs into the millions of euros.”

Van Houten said the rules were difficult to enforce because only importation is illegal. In the last year 500 inspections were carried out and 90 companies were given warnings, but only five were fined.

“It’s a drop in the ocean and it costs a lot of capacity because we need to do far-reaching, deep investigations,” he said.

World.title: Parents of euthanasia teen go to court over prosecution letter
World.content:
The parents of a 17-year-old girl who chose to die by euthanasia in 2023 due to incurable psychological suffering have gone to court to force public prosecutors to identify a group of doctors that wrote a damning letter about the case.

Their daughter Milou’s psychological struggles were documented in a 2023 documentary, which covered her wish to be granted the right to voluntary death and the aftermath that followed.

The case caused significant public controversy and a group of 14 doctors subsequently wrote a letter suggesting a criminal investigation should be launched against the parents and doctors involved in treating her.

They called on prosecutors to find out “to what extent those close to this vulnerable patient (…) influenced this young patient’s decision to choose euthanasia.” The writers of the letter did not know Milou or her personal background and had not spoken to her themselves.

Eight of the signatories of the letter are still unnamed. In a courtroom in The Hague on Tuesday, the mother of Milou recounted how that letter had led to daily threats and intimidation, requiring the police to guard their home.

“As a parent, losing your child and having to miss them forever is the worst thing that can happen to you,” the mother Mireille Verhoof told the court. “Being accused afterwards of inciting the death of your child or being complicit in her death is beyond description and unbearable.”

She also said her daughter had effectively been “abused” by anti-euthanasia campaigners, who dismissed their integrity to further a political agenda.

The family’s lawyer Richard Korver also said that the people behind the letter should not be able to use their professional authority to make serious accusations and at the same time claim anonymity, reported to Omroep Brabant.

The public prosecution department still does not want to release the names so as to avoid further conflict and ensure people can bring judicial complaints in confidence. It also disputes that the letter was meant as a formal request for criminal proceedings.

The federation of doctors KNMG also condemned the letter, describing it as “indecent and unacceptable.” The court’s decision on the release of the names is expected on September 3.

If you or someone close to you is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. In the Netherlands, call 113 or 0800-0113 (free) for 24/7 support, or visit 113.nl, where the chat service is available in English.

World.title: Dutch shops to stock more GM food after EU relaxes rules in 2028
World.content:
More genetically modified food is likely to appear in Dutch stores when rules on licensing and labelling are relaxed in two years’ time.

The European parliament passed a law before the summer recess allowing food retailers to stock products containing GM ingredients without labelling them as such, as long as they account for less than 1% of the contents.

The more flexible law was brought in to offset the effect of stricter limits on pesticides, which the EU wanted to halve by 2030, so that growers could use genetic modification to make their crops more resistant to parasites.

But two years ago the EU dropped the pesticides bill, which commission president Ursula von der Leyen said had become “a symbol of polarisation”, while still going ahead with the relaxation of GM rules.

Food products that have been significantly changed by genetic modification will still have to be licensed and labelled under the current rules.

Michelle Habets, a researcher at the Rathenau Institute, a science and technology think tank based in The Hague, said the more flexible rules risked undermining public confidence in supermarkets and other food retailers.

She told NOS she had spoken to dozens of consumers about the new law while it was passing through the European parliament. “Everyone agreed that genetically modified crops should be labelled,” she said.

“People admitted they don’t always study every label in the supermarket, but they think transparency is important, as is the freedom of choice for people who don’t want to eat those crops for whatever reason.”

Jeroen Candel, associate professor of food and agricultural policy at Wageningen University, said GM crops could bring benefits by reducing the need for pesticides, but added a note of caution.

“The new law is based on the idead that we can optimalise the current system of agriculture with new technology,” he said. “But if we do that, we are maintaining a system that is not sustainable in terms of climate and biodiversity.”

World.title: Polish government proposes middle-class tax cuts funded by increased rates for wealthiest

We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. The country is already under the EU's excessive deficit procedure, requiring it to take steps to bring public finances under greater control https://t.co/LNJ0YrP2Ge — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland launches tourism campaign featuring Lewandowski, Eisenberg and Rubik

Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 The city of Lublin in eastern Poland, which will be a European City of Culture in 2029, last year welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors, including over half a million from abroad. The city is known for its rich Jewish history, and featured prominently in the 2024 Oscar-nominated film A Real Pain, directed by and starring Eisenberg, whose ancestors were Jews from Lublin and the nearby town of Krasnystaw. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP within a decade, from about 5% now. The strategy includes creating a “Polish brand” through which internationally recognised athletes, artists, historical figures and products are showcased more prominently. Last month, the government appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. The city of Lublin in eastern Poland welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors in 2025. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The European Commission has granted approval for a consortium led by American transportation conglomerate FedEx to take over Polish delivery giant InPost in a deal worth €7.8 billion (33.7 billion zloty). InPost, which operates in France, Spain, the UK, Portugal, Italy and the Benelux countries, as well as in its home market, confirmed on Tuesday that it had received the green light from the EU for the deal, which was announced in February. If it goes through, the takeover will see a consortium made up of FedEx along with existing InPost investors, Advent, A&R, and PPF, purchase all of the company’s shares at a price of €15.60 each. Konsorcjum inwestorów, w którym jednym z uczestników jest amerykański @FedEx, uzyskało bezwarunkową zgodę KE na nabycie wszystkich akcji @InPostPL @RBrzoska https://t.co/F4AleTCViO — WNP.PL (@wnppl) August 18, 2026 The group behind the deal says the aim is to help InPost continue its recent rapid expansion. The firm will retain its name, branding and Polish headquarters. Founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska will remain in place, as well as being a major shareholder through A&R, which is his investment vehicle. The deal will see Advent, an American private equity firm, and FedEx each hold 37% of InPost. A&R would have 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. Currently, PPF holds 28.75%, A&R 12.49%, and Advent 6.5%. The initial offer period for the consortium’s takeover was due to end on 27 July. In its announcement today of EU approval, InPost noted that it is still awaiting a green light from the Vietnam Competition Commission but expects a decision to be made by 8 September. Although the Polish company has no operations in Vietnam, FedEx has been present on the market since 1994. InPost has grown rapidly in recent years through its pioneering use of parcel lockers, first in Poland and then across western Europe. In the UK, it has established a network of over 14,000 parcel lockers, including in branches of the British Post Office. In June this year, French President Emannuel Macron thanked InPost for its latest investment in France, where the firm – which operates there through its subsidiary Mondial Relay – is planning to spend a further €500 million to expand its presence. World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July.
